News.title: Murder probe launched after man, 24, ‘stabbed to death’ in the street as man, 27, arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KNIFE 'ATTACK' Murder probe launched after man, 24, ‘stabbed to death’ in the street as man, 27, arrested

A 27-YEAR-OLD man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a 24-year-old man was stabbed to death.

Emergency services were called to the scene in Levenshulme, Manchester, at around 7pm, yesterday evening.

Despite the best efforts of paramedics a 24-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene.

He had suffered serious knife wounds.





A 27-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder and remains in custody at this time.

Greater Manchester Police said work was ongoing to locate the victim’s next of kin.

Detective Inspector Alex Wilkinson from our Major Incident Team said: “Our thoughts are with the family and friends of the victim in this tragic incident.

“Officers acted swiftly to arrest a man, who is in our custody for questioning.



“Our investigation is ongoing and we would like to hear from anyone who may have information that can assist us.

“Anyone in the Chapel Street area around the time of this incident, or who has mobile phone, CCTV, Ring doorbell and dashcam footage, can contact police on 0161 856 9008 quoting the log number 2983 of 15/08/2026.

“Alternatively contact independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: One dead and two kids, 4 & 14, among multiple injured in horrific shooting at outdoor concert in Kentucky
News.content:
GUN HORROR One dead and two kids, 4 & 14, among multiple injured in horrific shooting at outdoor concert in Kentucky

ONE person has been killed and four others are injured in a mass shooting at a concert in Kentucky.

Two children, one aged four and another 14, are among those wounded in downtown Lexington, on Saturday evening.

Gunfire broke out during a concert in Charles Young Park, sending people running for their lives.



A Facebook livestream showed the moment the very first shots were fired and the chaos erupting.



A group of teenagers can be seen instinctively ducking for cover before fleeing the scene, while others were shown dropping to the ground in the hope to escape the bullets whistling past them.

The video ends with a person lying on the grass as multiple people race to help them, but it is unclear if they were injured.

All victims were taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

News.title: Moment woman brazenly walks out of nail salon ‘to get cash’ for £85 bill before climbing into waiting car & driving off
News.content:
THIS is the moment a woman brazenly walks out of a nail salon “to get cash” for her £85 bill before reportedly clambering into a waiting car and driving off.

Hope Tran, who owns the New Milton Nails salon in the New Forest, Hampshire, said she was left having to pick up the tab.



The shameless woman had been pampered for two hours with acrylic infills with colour tips, costing £35 and a full pedicure with removal and colour tips, priced at £50.

She was dressed in pink with sunglasses perched on her head and was wearing white sliders and even enjoyed a cup of coffee on the house.



CCTV footage from the salon shows her scrolling on her phone as a member of staff works on her nails.

Despite the signs stating the salon did not accept card payments, the woman still asked to settle her bill this way.

She then said she would go to the cash machine opposite the beauty bar.

Flabbergasted staff allegedly watched her as she walked straight towards a blue car parked outside and hopped in without paying.



The woman was believed to be a holidaymaker staying at a nearby campsite.

However, with no information to go on in order to trace the woman, Hope was reportedly left having to foot the bill.

The salon owner said: “As soon as she came in I had a bad feeling.

“She had a strong accent and mentioned she had been camping, hence she was all covered in mud.

“She went to the toilet to use our cleaning brush to brush off her slider.



“I even offered her coffee and she asked me what it was as she liked it.

“At the end she asked if she could pay by card, I told her we don’t have a card reader and said she could do a bank transfer or cash.

“She asked to go to the cash machine across the road.”

Hope added: “I watched her walk across the road but instead of going to the cash machine she got straight into a blue car that was already parked and waiting for her right beside the cash machine and they drove off.

“I still had to pay my hard-working staff who did her nails for over two hours, meaning they could not do any other paying clients during that time.



‘”I have to use my own money to cover all her costs – nail products, electric, water.

“In the future I think I will have to ask for payment upfront for holidaymakers and first time clients.

“Hopefully it won’t happen again.”

She added she hadn’t bothered telling the police as she didn’t think they could do anything.

The customer’s face was shared on social media by one of Hope’s clients in the hope that someone might recognise her and shame her into doing the right thing.



One commenter said: “You madam are a disgrace, do you know how businesses are struggling how Hope the owner works so hard?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You probably don’t care because you feel entitled – you’re just a thieving low life.”

Another added: “No small business can afford this, people who do this are complete lowlifes.”

News.title: Shoppers evacuated as blaze breaks out near Tesco superstore as locals warned to stay away amid fears of ‘toxic fumes’
News.content:
SHOPPERS have been evacuated after a massive blaze broke out near a Tesco superstore with locals warned to stay away amid fears of toxic fumes.

Emergency services raced to the scene on an industrial estate in Oldham, Greater Manchester, earlier this morning.



Shocking footage circulating on social media, taken from a Tesco superstore car park, shows a towering plume of black smoke billowing into the sky.

Local residents have been urged avoid the area and to keep their windows and doors closed while a cordon is also in place.



The blaze appears to be just behind the supermarket with ten fire crews descending on the scene to battle the inferno.

The store has been temporarily closed while a specialist environmental unit has arrived with reports there are toxic materials at the location.



People have been evacuated from the area amid reports there are toxic fumes coming from the industrial site.

A spokesperson for Tesco said: “Our Greenfield Superstore is temporarily closed due to a fire nearby. We apologise for the inconvenience.”

Shocking photos show firefighters tackling the flames on a hydraulic platform from above.

In a statement, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said: “Just after 7.45am on Sunday 16 August, fire crews were called to reports of a fire at an industrial building on Chew Valley Road, Greenfield.”



“10 fire engines and a number of specialist appliances from across Greater Manchester are now in attendance, with firefighters working hard to bring the fire under control.

“Due to the amount of smoke, nearby residents are advised to keep their windows and doors closed.

“A cordon is in place and people should avoid the area if possible.”

The Sun has contacted Greater Manchester Police for comment.

News.title: The suicide drone onslaught shattering Putin’s ‘Amazon’ empire as Ukraine plots next death blow to paralyse war machine
News.content:
UKRAINE’S daring and destructive drone attacks shattering Vladimir Putin’s Amazon-style empire have thrown the Kremlin’s economy into freefall.

A dozen Wildberries warehouses have been blitzed in the past month with Kyiv now plotting for their next death blow against Moscow to further paralyse Putin’s faltering war machine.



Longtime Kremlin critic and Brit banker Bill Browder told The Sun: “These attacks on the Wildberries warehouses are a combination of economic, military and psychological war on the Russians.”

Wildberries, Russia’s largest online marketplace, was first targeted on July 18, as Ukraine unleashed a sustained attack around Moscow across 48 hours.



Several major sites were struck with warehouses left smoking across the weary capital.

Strikes then hit further hubs in St Petersburg, Crimea and multiple other cities.



At least 12 Wildberries hubs have been sent up in flames since late July – plunging one of Russia‘s most crucial businesses into disarray.

Ex-British intelligence officer Philip Ingram told The Sun: “Ukrainians seem to be hitting two or three warehouses every couple of days and burning them down and destroying them.”



One of the most important sites hit so far by Ukrainian suicide drones is a warehouse in the Urals Mountains city of Yekaterinburg, Philip added.

He said: “Yekaterinburg sits 2,000km from the Ukrainian border but we’ve seen drones be able to get through Russian air defence capabilities the whole way and hit a site there.

“If we look at the air defences out there, the military planning and intelligence that’s needed to do that is phenomenal.

“Russia can’t protect its capital city. It can’t protect its second city and it can’t stop Ukrainian drones hitting 2,000km away on the other side of the Urals.

“So what can Russia protect? Its emboldening the Ukrainians. It’s worrying the Russians and it’s causing Vladimir Putin a massive headache.”



There are a total of 40 sprawling Wildberries warehouses with another 200 smaller facilities spread out across Russia.

Thousands of national retailers regularly use Wildberries to buy and store their goods as well as using the brand’s delivery service.

Even Russian troops rely on the supplier for helmets and armour before they head to the bloody battlefield.



In 2025, Wildberries’ turnover was recorded at £58.5bn, almost three per cent of Russia’s gross domestic product and nearly half of its online retail figures.

This makes it a vital economic powerhouse in Russia which helps prop up the Kremlin with a steady cash flow.

“This is where Ukraine is playing a longer term game,” Philip warned.

Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky and his war chiefs have been fighting on the back foot since Putin’s launched his full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Russia has a vastly superior number of troops and powerful weapons in their arsenal compared to Ukraine even with US and Nato‘s support.



This has pushed Kyiv to carry out more technical assaults away from the frontline including the attacks on Wildberries.

How Ukraine’s cunning tactic to blitz ‘Russia’s Amazon’ could deal fatal blow to Putin’s regime By Harvey Geh, Foreign News Reporter AFTER weeks of blitzing Vladimir Putin’s oil depots with state-of-the-art drones, Ukraine has now shifted its crosshairs to Russia’s Amazon. In another bid to bring the tyrant to the negotiating table, Kyiv is putting its foot on Moscow’s neck with a series of strikes crippling the regime’s biggest e-commerce platform. The despot could be staring down the barrel of a mutiny by the time key elections come round in September if Ukraine keeps its foot on the gas and Moscow continues to struggle against aerial assaults, experts say. Russia expert Mark Galeotti told The Sun: “The Ukrainians have been extraordinarily and unexpectedly successful, and this is slowly grinding away… at support for the regime bit by bit.” And John Foreman CBE, former UK Defence Attaché to Russia, said: “The strategy… is to inflict pain inside Russia, inside the occupied territories, inside Crimea, to bring home the cost of war back to Russians.” Russia analyst Natia Seskuria told us: “It’s a very smart strategy from the Ukrainian side… it will have a significant impact on Russian households.” She added: “This is something new and something that we haven’t seen before, but I think the message is still the same in terms of making the war extremely costly for Russia.” READ MORE HERE

Philip continued: “Kyiv is recognising that on the battlefield all it can do is hold the Russians back because they’re much stronger militarily.

“So instead it’s attacking at an operational level. Attacking Russia’s very core ability to continue to support the operations and the people that will be going on the front line.”

Philip said Ukraine’s plan is clear, to “undermine Vladimir Putin from a political perspective, and undermine Russia from an economic perspective internally.”



Philip continued: “Ukraine’s strategy is evolving, the hits on Wildberries and the general oil and gas infrastructure are causing a financial burden to Moscow.

“It is bringing the war home to the average Russian.

“The civilian population is now fearing the government can’t protect them anymore.

“They can’t protect their businesses due to the Wildberries attacks and the cost of living is going through the roof.”

Bill agreed, saying “bringing the war home” to the Russians is “probably the most important thing that they’re doing”.



The move will create pressure on Putin and the government by hampering their ability to justify the war.

“The less justification they have, the less sacrifice the average Russian is going to want to make and perhaps at some point the wave of indignation in Russia becomes unbearable for Putin”, Bill said.

Bill believes there are two logical next steps for the Ukrainians after seeing the huge success they’ve had with striking Wildberries.

They could attack the next largest goods supplier in the country, known as Ozone, as many people have just started to buy and sell through their stores now instead.

In a similar vein, Ukraine’s blistering attacks on oil and gas refineries could show where Kyiv might hit next.



Bill said: “Wherever the most economic activity is in Russia should be the target.

“And so if they’re targeting oil refineries and crippling the cash exports they might soon move onto targeting metals exports.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“That’s another big source of income for the Russian economy.

“Anywhere that the Ukrainians can find where there’s economic flows going to the Russian economy into the government should be fair game.”

News.title: Woman in her 60s arrested for ‘murder & arson’ after woman in her 90s dies in early morning house fire
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FIRE HORROR Woman in her 60s arrested for ‘murder & arson’ after woman in her 90s dies in early morning house fire

A WOMAN in her 60s has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman in her 90s was found dead following a fire in the early hours.

Emergency services were scrambled to an address in Hardwick, Gloucestershire, shortly before 4am, after receiving reports of a fire.

Fire crews, ambulance and police responded to the scene and the inferno was brought under control.

The property was searched and a woman in her 90s was found unconscious inside.





Emergency services performed CPR but despite their best efforts, the woman was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

Her next of kin has been informed.

A woman aged in her 60s and from Gloucester has since been arrested in connection with the incident.

She was taken into custody on suspicion of murder and arson with intent to endanger life.

She remains in police custody for questioning at this time.

A cordon remains in place around the scene as investigators probe the tragedy.

Gloucestershire Constabulary said: “Police would like to reassure the public that those involved in the incident are known to each other and this appears to have been an isolated incident.”

News.title: Two women killed & 2 babies injured after devastating flash flood triggered landslide in Spain with search op launched
News.content:
TWO women have been killed and two babies have been injured after a devastating flash flood and landslide caused by torrential rain in Spain.

An urgent search operation has been launched for missing locals as weather warnings for severe downpours have also been issued.



The two women, aged 60 and 80, were confirmed dead in the Castile and Leon region after biblical rain on Saturday.

A sweeping deluge hit the village of Manzanedo de Valdueza, near Pontevedra.



This triggered overflowing in the Orza River which then sparked flash flooding and a landslide.

Two babies were treated for bruises during the horror weather conditions.



The two youngsters and two elderly victims were in a winery alongside two survivors when floodwater started seeping into the room.

Shocking footage has also shown the extent of the floods – with muddy water seen rushing through cars as rain pummels the streets.



Some vehicles were swept away during the extraordinary storm, reports say.

In another clip, stunned locals watched on as an overflowing river swept away piles of debris, seemingly from a landslide.

The jaw-dropping weather has damaged roads and cut off several links between towns.

Firefighters, police and emergency workers have all been deployed to help locals.

Spain‘s Civil ⁠Protection today warned of upcoming storms and heavy ​rain in seven regions ​of ⁠central and northern Spain.



The flooding warnings follow weeks of record-breaking heatwaves that have sparked huge wildfires across the country.

It comes after a brutal storm struck the Costa del Sol with torrential rain and hailstones sparking a flood alert in the Brit holiday hotspot.

Urgent weather warnings were issued across Spain‘s southern coast on Saturday as thunderstorms wreaked havoc.

Shocked holidaymakers arriving at Malaga Airport in the early hours of Saturday morning were met with heavy rain and powerful gusts of wind.

News.title: Body of missing man, 62, discovered at house as cops arrest man for ‘murder’ & beauty spot trail cordoned off
News.content:
TRAGIC END Body of missing man, 62, discovered at house as cops arrest man for ‘murder’ & beauty spot trail cordoned off

THE body of a missing man has been discovered inside a property – as cops arrest a man on suspicion of murder and a beauty spot trail is cordoned off.

Police had received reports of a missing 62-year-old man from Sheffield, South Yorkshire, on Friday evening.



Five hours later, at around 10.16pm, cops were then called to reports of a body inside a property on George Street in Barnsley.

Emergency services scrambled to the scene where they discovered the man who was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.



South Yorkshire Police said his family are now being supported by specialist officers.

The force has now launched a murder probe and a 60-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder.



He currently remains in police custody.

Cops have put three scenes in place while investigations get underway with two currently in place on George Street and another on the TransPennine trial nearby.

Detective Chief Inspector Aneela Khalil-Khan, who is currently leading the investigation, said: “This news will be shocking to the local communities, and not something they expect to be waking up to on a Saturday morning.

“Our officers have moved fast, and have made an arrest. They are now working hard to determine the circumstances around this tragic incident.



“Our officers will be around the Worsbrough area of Barnsley throughout the day and into the evening, conducting several lines of enquiries.

“This is distressing news, so please stop and talk to them if you have some concerns – they will listen and help where they can.”

The force added they had also referred themselves to the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) as is “standard protocol” as the man had previously been reported missing.

Anyone with information is urged to come forward to police by calling 101 or reporting it to the force online, quoting incident number 1238 of 14 August 2026.

News.title: An IED tore off ex-Gurkha Hari Budha Magar's legs but the hero fought back and conquered Everest
News.content:
NEAR the roof of the world, they were already writing his obituary - but Hari Budha Magar had other ideas. High on Everest, in the dark, out of oxygen, Hari was a dead man as far as the people who loved him were concerned. A double above the knee amputee, after an IED tore off both his legs in Afghanistan, he had fought back against all odds to conquer Everest.

But now a broken satellite call over a screaming wind had been misheard, and the men below believed that for all his bravery, hope was lost. Hari said: "They were sitting in their tents, planning what to say, because they thought we were already dead.”

Out of oxygen at more than eight thousand metres he understood exactly what that meant, saying: "You can offer a man a million pounds for his oxygen at that altitude and he will refuse. “Money is worthless when you are about to die."

View 7 Images Hari Budha Mahgar the Pride of Britain winner who is the first double amputee to have conquered the Seven Summits (Image: Adam Gerrard / Mirror Books)

‌



Hari's determination and will to survive was formed from an early age. Born in a cowshed in a Nepali village on 30 July 1979, his birth was difficult and he came into the world silent, with his parents feeling he wasn't going to live. But the old woman who delivered him said: "Of course he's alive. Full of energy! He will be a climber this one, I can feel it."

Hari's obsession started in a hot classroom, when a teacher paced the front of the room and asked: "What does Sagarmatha mean to you?" It is Nepali name for Everest. "My mind exploded with questions: What about me climbing? How do people climb? How would it feel to stand on top?" Hari said.

But he put his dreams on hold to join the British Army, completing its gruelling Gurkha selection in December 1998. As a Gurkha, he served for more than ten years, rising through the ranks. On the night before his company flew into Helmand in Afhghanistan, he made himself a promise - to serve the Crown, protect his platoon, and fight to his last breath if he had to.

View 7 Images Hari Budha Magar with his wife and their three children Ubran, Brian and Samjhana.

‌



On the 17 April 2010, in the Nahr-e-Seraj district of Helmand, the work in hand was the unglamorous business of rebuilding, not fighting. He said: "I walked across a poppy field to help repair a village's well: civilian infrastructure work, not a combat operation.”

Then there was a bang and the world tilted onto its side. When the dust settled and he forced his neck to bend, the damage was plain. "My right leg, it just isn't there. It's gone," he said. And where his left leg should have been there was only "a dangling of bone and skin." Lying in the dirt, he thought: "Am I going to survive? Will I be able to see my family again?"

He was the tenth man in a single-file patrol when he stepped on the device, and for a few desperate minutes no one could reach him, while the ground around him was swept for more hidden bombs. Hari’s own men applied field dressings, and 18 minutes after the blast he was carried on an improvised stretcher to an American rescue helicopter.

View 7 Images Hari Budha Magar at Everest Base Camp in 2022

‌



Hari came home to Britain without his legs, but the mental toll was as bad as the physical. First came the surgery and the slow repair - a month in Selly Oak hospital in Birmingham and then three and a half years of rehabilitation at Headley Court in Surrey. But PTSD had taken hold.

He said: "I wake up in cold sweats. I hear the thunderous BANG! of the explosion, replaying again and again and again in my head.” For months he sat in a wheelchair by the window. The only relief was drinking and he fell into alcoholism. He said: "The only time I felt anything was after the whisky. The emptiness was the worst part. For the first time in my life I felt like I had no tribe, no cause, nothing filled in the calendar. I had no purpose."

What pulled him back was a single reckless afternoon in the summer of 2012, when the army's Battle Back scheme offered wounded veterans a day's skydiving. Hari signed up for the bleakest of reasons. He said: "Half of my body is gone, if the other goes then it's the end of my story.

View 7 Images Hari Budha Magar is made a Member of the Order of the British Empire by the Princess Royal at Windsor Castle (Image: PA)

‌



At Netheravon Airfield in Wiltshire, he was fully prepared for the parachute to fail. At the open door of the plane, 15,000 feet up, he remembered an old Gurkha saying: "It's better to die than be a coward." And he jumped out into the sky. He said: "The first time after my injury, I felt I was free like a bird.”

After that, Hari threw himself into adaptive sport, won medals, kayaked around the Isle of Wight and, on ski trips in the Alps, he began to dream of climbing Everest again. His own government tried to stop him. Nepal brought in a ban on double amputees attempting its highest peaks. "It was clear that what now awaited me was not a mountain climb at all, it was another challenge," he said. "It was a fight."

The fight went all the way to Nepal's Supreme Court and the ban was overturned - meaning he was free to take on Everest. Hari’s ascent had been tougher than the normal climb, as his disability meant he had to spend three times as much energy as an able-bodied climber.

The Hillary Step at 28,700 feet nearly finished him. He said: "My lungs were on fire. I almost collapsed." Above it, the summit finally showed itself through his frozen goggles.

‌



View 7 Images Hari Budha Magar (second left), meets Sir Keir Starmer at 10 Downing Street with his family after winning the Daily Mirror Pride of Britain Awards' Special Recognition Award in 2024 (Image: Tim Merry/Staff Photographer)

Hari crawled the last of it, stopping every step to breathe, before planting his palms on the top of the world on 19 May 2023. He said: "Tears spilt down my cheeks like waterfalls and froze like stalagmites hanging from my eyelashes. I wanted to let every human no longer look upon persons with disability as pitiful or limited or weak."

On his descent, the oxygen ran out, the torch died, the water and the food froze solid. His guide, Mingma, gave away his own oxygen and stumbled into Camp Four half dead. And a Sherpa, Pasang, who had never been that high in his life, climbed up through the night carrying two bottles and a flask of hot water to find them. Hari said: "It was warm and it was wet and it meant we were going to live." The climb, top to bottom, had taken 25 hours.

View 7 Images Hari Budha Magar's book Conquering Dreams

‌



In 2024, he was awarded an MBE in the King's Birthday Honours for services to disability awareness, and later that year he won a Pride of Britain Award and was invited with his family to Downing Street. Everest was never the end of it. Hari has since completed the Seven Summits, the highest peak on every continent - including Antarctica., the world's first double above the knee amputee to do so.

Hari, now 47, is honest about how hard ordinary life remains, but he keeps going - determined to set an example of bravery and leadership. "I might not change the whole world," he said, "but if I can help just one person change their life for the better, I will be happy."

*Conquering Dreams by Hari Budha Magar (Mirror Books) is published August 27th, priced £16.99

News.title: 'Pins and needles turned out to be deadly spiderweb in my brain'
News.content:
'Pins and needles turned out to be deadly spiderweb in my brain'

EXCLUSIVE: Mum-of-five Bryony Hill from Selston, Nottinghamshire, is living on borrowed time after receiving a devastating diagnosis after what initially seemed to be a minor problem

View 7 Images Bryony was given dreadful news after undergoing an MRI scan (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

A mum claims doctors dismissed her pins and needles as an old rock climbing injury - before they found terminal brain cancer had made a 'spiderweb' in her head.

‌



Bryony Hill says she first visited her GP in September 2025 with concerns of headaches and that she had a 'lumpy skull', and was simply given migraine medication.

‌



When the mum-of-five began suffering ankle pain in October she visited A&E and claims she was told she had tendonitis thanks to breaking her ankle while rock climbing 18 years earlier.

‌



View 7 Images The mum of five has an incurable tumour (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

Jason Arday funeral fundraiser tops £50,000 after tragic death in Cambridge plagiarism scandal READ MORE :

Horrors of Grenfell Tower blaze leave THIRTY fire brigade staff suffering PTSD READ MORE :

But the stay-at-home mum says the 'tingling' in her right foot eventually got worse and spread through the right side of her body, so in in April 2026 she was referred for an MRI.

Whilst waiting for the scan, Bryony's husband James Hill, 42, had planned a trip away for her 40th birthday in May but the day before she woke up after having a seizure and was rushed to hospital.

‌



There an emergency MRI revealed Bryony had a brain tumour and following a biopsy she received the devastating news that she had stage 4 glioblastoma, which is inoperable due to it spreading like a 'spiderweb'.

View 7 Images An MRI scan revealed the awful truth (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

Glioblastomas are the most common and most malignant primary brain tumour, which usually spread quickly to other parts of the brain and so are difficult to treat.

‌



Bryony, who is from Selston, Nottinghamshire, said: "I went to the doctors last year and I had quite a few headaches and I just went and spoke about that and I did mention while I was there that I felt like I had a lumpy skull.

"I mentioned it to my doctor at the time and he prescribed me some medication because I was having migraines. I've got an older break in my ankle from 18 years ago so on my right side I have screws in my ankle.

View 7 Images She had spoken to her husband about having difficulties (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

‌



"I randomly had a really bad pain on my ankle and I couldn't walk on it so I went to the doctors about it in A&E. They just thought it was tendonitis and they were like 'oh well have some crutches, take some medicine but we can't really see any problems.'

"It was April this year I got a tingling in my foot. It just started to feel tingly and I had already given it four weeks [since the A&E visit] before coming into the doctors.

"The tingling was just getting worse and I mentioned [to doctors] that I'd got a previous fracture, I'd been treated for tendonitis. The doctor decided to book me in for an MRI."

‌



View 7 Images A doctor ordered her to undergo a scan (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

According to the NHS, tendonitis is often caused by an injury and is when the tissue connecting muscles to bones swells and causes pain and stiffness.

The NHS also states that symptoms of brain tumours vary depending on where in the brain they are situated but one of the symptoms is progressive weakness or paralysis on one side of the body.

‌



Bryony said: "If I dropped something on the floor, I wouldn't be able to feel it because all I was getting was pins and needles. It was just getting worse and further up my body.

"It got to a point where I had to stop driving for safety reasons because I was like 'I can't feel my leg.' My husband had arranged for us to go on holiday for May half term for my 40th birthday.

View 7 Images The scan revealed the extent of the tumour (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

‌



"We were going to go the next day so on May 21 I went to bed that night, I woke up in the early hours to ambulance men around my head and I was coming in and out of consciousness because I had no idea what had happened and I had had a seizure. Then they discovered that I've got the tumour."

Bryony claims that initially it was believed her tumour was grade two but after receiving a biopsy doctors confirmed that it was grade four. She says her tumour 'diffuses' into her central nervous system like a 'spiderweb' so doctors are unable to remove it.

Due to it being incurable, Bryony's family have set up a fundraiser to help pay for alternative treatment abroad to give her more time with her family.

‌



You can donate to Bryony's fundraiser here: https://www.gofundme.com/f/young-mum-of-5-children-with-inoperable-brain-tumor

Bryony said: "My husband is on the internet every day trying to find anything and everything that can prolong life as much as possible. I've got five children that I'll be leaving behind, time is very precious, any extra time is huge.

View 7 Images Bryony and her family want to make the most of the time she has left (Image: KENNEDY NEWS & MEDIA)

‌



"The type that I have is more like a spiderweb so it diffuses into your central nervous system so it wants to spread out like spiderwebs rather than being a removable chunk. It's not really anything you can poke around and do too much with because of the location.

"It's grade four and there is only so much they can do for that. It looks like a grade two on the outside but internally it's a grade four. They can't take it out, it's the worst type, it's the most aggressive. It just happened so fast.

"There's just so much I can't do, even just playing with my daughter. I can't get up and run to her."

Article continues below

A spokesperson for the NHS Derby and Derbyshire Integrated Care Board on behalf of the GP surgery said: "We are unable to discuss individual cases, to protect patient confidentiality.

"We would encourage all patients to make contact with the practice to discuss any concerns they may have about their care."

News.title: Harwich fire - live: Huge blaze fills sky with smoke as people told 'shut windows'
News.content:
Huge flames and plumes of smoke can be seen coming from the fire at a warehouse on Stour Road in Harwich with residents told to keep doors and windows closed

A massive fire is ripping through a warehouse near the Essex coast with smoke pouring from the building and people living nearby warned to keep doors and windows and closed.

Flames can be seen coming from the fire in Harwich as emergency services battle the fire in Stour Road this morning.

Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said: "Thank you to everyone who has rung our Control Room to let us know about the fire on Stour Road in Harwich.

"Our crews are at the scene and are working to extinguish a warehouse that is alight. There is a lot of smoke coming from the incident, if you live nearby please keep all your windows and doors shut."

News.title: Virgin Atlantic engineer, 23, killed after explosion at Heathrow was 'beautiful son'
News.content:
Virgin Atlantic engineer, 23, killed after explosion at Heathrow was 'beautiful son'

Virgin engineer Georgie Buxton died from a traumatic brain injury after an explosion as he worked inside a plane fuel tank

View Image Georgie Buxton died when he was crushed by machinery at Heathrow Airport (Image: Jam Press/Rachel Buxton/GoFundMe)

A family has paid tribute to their "beautiful son" who died after suffering a traumatic brain injury following an explosion as he worked on a plane fuel tank.

‌



Aircraft technician Georgie Buxton, 23, was injured during the incident at Heathrow Airport on 11 June and underwent various surgeries to his head and neck but could not be saved.

‌



Georgie had been working for Virgin Atlantic for two years and had previously held the same role with Ryanair.

‌



Now his family have revealed their heartbreak in a fundraising appeal. Rachel Buxton said on GoFundMe that Georgie was a "kind, intelligent and caring young man who had so much to look forward to".

M9 crash horror as multiple dead and four injured including child in County Kildare READ MORE :

She said: "He had recently started his career as an Aircraft Technician with Virgin Atlantic, a role he was incredibly proud of and which reflected his passion for engineering and aviation.

"He had quickly become a much-loved and highly respected member of his team. Following the accident, the London Air Ambulance team gave Georgie the chance to survive.

‌



"Without their rapid response and specialist care, he would not have made it to hospital. Georgie spent the next 27 days in the Intensive Care Unit at St Mary's Hospital.

"During that time, the doctors, nurses and ICU team did everything possible to save him. Their skill, dedication and compassion were extraordinary, and they supported not only Georgie but our whole family through the most devastating time of our lives.

"Sadly, despite everything they did, Georgie's injuries were too severe and he passed away after 27 days in ICU."

‌



Georgie's colleague, who was in another part of the fuel tank and avoided injury, managed to move him from the tank on to the platform stairs they were using.

A forensic post-mortem examination carried out at the request of police found that Georgie had suffered a traumatic brain injury – a craniofacial trauma.

A criminal investigation has been launched by the Metropolitan Police who are working with the Health and Safety Executive.

‌



An inquest into Georgie's death was opened and suspended pending any criminal charges being brought.

The family are raising money in Georgie's memory for London Air Ambulance and St Mary's Hospital ICU.

They said: "London Air Ambulance is a charity and relies on funding to continue its life-saving work.

‌



"St Mary's Hospital is part of our incredible NHS, and the ICU team are fundraising to improve facilities and better support families during the most difficult times.

"Georgie filled our lives with love, laughter and immense pride. His life was far too short, but the impact he made on everyone who knew him will last forever.

"If you are able to donate, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. If you can't, sharing Georgie's story would mean just as much. For Georgie, and for the teams who never stopped fighting for him."

Article continues below

At the time of writing, the fundraising page had raised £26,604. You can donate to the fundraiser here.

News.title: Hollywood star Shane Ryan Gledhill faces 24 child sex abuse charges after 'using cast calls as bait'
News.content:
Hollywood star Shane Ryan Gledhill faces 24 child sex abuse charges after 'using cast calls as bait'

Hollywood actor and producer Shane Ryan Gledhill has been hit with a total of 24 felony charges relating to allegations of child sexual abuse and has been accused of using casting calls to lure his victims

View 3 Images Hollywood actor and producer Shane Ryan Gledhill has been hit with a total of 24 felony charges relating to allegations of child sexual abuse (Image: Santa Barbara Sheriff)

Shane Ryan Gledhill is facing a total of 24 felony charges relating to allegations of child sexual abuse. The actor, 46, also known as Shane Ryan-Reid, has been accused of using his internet casting calls and film projects to find underage victims.

‌



The actor and producer, who over the course of his career has worked with A-listers including Shelley Duvall, Richard Dreyfuss, and Kathryn Eastwood, was arrested in Lompoc on August 3 by Santa Barbara County officials and initially faced 15 counts of child sexual abuse, but that number later increased to 24.

‌



Amongst the charges are child molestation, rape, forcible sexual assault, possession of child sexual abuse material, and contacting a minor with the intent to commit a sexual offence.

‌



View 3 Images The actor seen here in Deadly Western, was the subject of a five-year investigation (Image: Deadly Western – Epoch Cinema)

His arrest follows a five-year investigation, and police have said they believe there may be more survivors out there who are not known to them at present.

Police said: "Investigators believe Gledhill’s alleged criminal conduct may have spanned approximately 25 years and involved individuals throughout the Central Coast, the Los Angeles area, and potentially the East Coast through his filmmaking and casting activities."

‌



Police also pointed out that those who interacted with the man in question may not recognise his legal name because he often used the name Shane Ryan-Reid or Shane Ryan when contacting his victims.

The investigation into Gledhill began in November 2021, when a 17-year-old reported "suspicious and inappropriate conduct" between her and the producer that she claimed had occurred two years earlier.

Police said: "During the initial investigation, detectives identified two additional survivors. Over the course of the investigation, detectives identified nine survivors, all of whom were minors at the time of the alleged offences."

‌



View 3 Images The producer, seen her in Shadow Death, is currently being held in jail (Image: Epoch Cinema)

Months later, his home in Lompoc, California, was searched, and thousands of digital files were analysed by forensic experts. Currently, Gledhill is being held at Northern Branch Jail, and bail has been set at $500,000.

One of the films from Gledhill's back catalogue is titled Warning!!! Pedophile, which he produced and starred in, sees him play a man who has just got out of prison after serving six years for molesting a 12-year-old girl. Another film, which is still listed as being in pre-production, is titled The Victim and follows a girl who is being held accountable for a man's suicide after she accused him of abuse.

Article continues below

According to his IMDB page, Gledhill has worked as a producer on almost 250 projects and, early on in his career, appeared in popular TV series such as The OC, Desperate Housewives and Disney Channel hit That's So Raven.

If you've been the victim of sexual assault, you can access help and resources via www.rapecrisis.org.uk or calling the national telephone helpline on 0808 802 9999

For more of the latest showbiz news and gossip, follow Mirror Celebs on TikTok , Snapchat , Instagram , Twitter , Facebook , YouTube and Threads .

News.title: 'Clean any room' Aldi's new £40 gadget similar to Dyson and Shark - out Thursday
News.content:
'Clean any room' Aldi's new £40 gadget similar to Dyson and Shark - out Thursday

Shoppers can "power through dust, dirt, and debris" with the new Special Buy deal

View 3 Images The new gadget will be coming out in a few days (Image: Getty )

Aldi is releasing a new Special Buy offer in its Middle Aisle next week that could be a budget-friendly alternative for anyone who likes Dyson and Shark-style products, but doesn't want to spend more than they need to. The supermarket updates its Special Buy offerings every Sunday and Thursday, with the next round of items coming out in a few days.

‌



On Thursday, August 20, the supermarket will be bringing back its Ambiano Cyclonic Stick Vacuum Cleaner as part of a new collection of 'Student Home' goods. The range is aimed at people returning to, or starting, university in September, to help make juggling chores, studying and socialising 'easier'.

‌



The Cyclonic Stick Vacuum Cleaner costs £39.99 and is available in either black or white. It comes with a DC motor and a 180-degree swivel head. It also has a run time of up to 32 minutes and comes with a motorised brush and three LED lights.

‌



Aldi says the vacuum cleaner is designed to help clean any room. In the product description, it explains: "Power through dust, dirt, and debris with the Cyclonic Stick Vacuum Cleaner. Lightweight, powerful, and easy to manoeuvre, it delivers deep cleaning performance on every floor."

View 3 Images Ambiano Cyclonic Stick Vacuum Cleaner (Image: Aldi)

However, as with any Special Buy deal, stock is limited, so when it's gone, it is gone. The £39.99 vacuum cleaner could be a budget-friendly alternative to Dyson and Shark models, which share similar features but cost more.

‌



The £39.99 vacuum cleaner shares features with Dyson's V8 Cordless Vacuum, which is on sale at retailers such as Currys and John Lewis for £239. Like Dyson, Aldi's Ambiano Cyclonic Stick Vacuum Cleaner features a lightweight, bagless design and comes with attachments, all at a lower price.

Both vacuums share a modern, lightweight cordless stick design that includes a detachable handheld section and interchangeable nozzles. They are both bagless cyclonic systems that can clean multiple surfaces, including hard floors and low-pile rugs.

View 3 Images Aldi updates its Special Buy offers every Thursday and Sunday (stock image)

Article continues below

Opinions on Reddit are mixed; some users claim that while the Ambiano is great for quick clean-ups or smaller areas, it lacks the powerful motor, larger bin capacity, or long-lasting battery life in high mode that a Dyson offers. Reddit users generally agree that budget store-brand stick vacuums tend to have more plastic parts and a shorter lifespan compared to premium brand-name models.

Aldi's £39.99 vacuum cleaner could also be compared to Shark's Stratos Cordless Stick Vacuum, which costs £229.99 at Argos. Both have a similar light, upright design and a detachable handheld option.

But Aldi's model is said to have lower suction power and doesn't include the advanced anti-hair-wrap rollers.

News.title: Rapists and child sex offenders to face pinpoint tagging in biggest ever monitoring expansion
News.content:
Rapists and child sex offenders to face pinpoint tagging in biggest ever monitoring expansion

The Ministry of Justice has announced that rapists and child sex offenders will face round-the-clock real-time tagging after serving their full prison term in the biggest ever expansion of electronic monitoring

View 2 Images Released sex offenders will face round-the-clock electronic tagging for at least a year (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Rapists and child sex offenders will face round-the-clock real-time tagging after serving their full prison term in the biggest ever expansion of electronic monitoring.

‌



The government announced sex offenders will be monitored by GPS - which pins down their precise location - for at least a year after their release. It comes after Andy Burnham announced rapists and those guilty of child sex and grooming crimes will not be included in the controversial prisoner early release scheme.

‌



This means they will not come out of prison a moment before they were due to. A new £700million package will use new tracking technology to monitor released sex offenders' movements. It means police and probation will be able to act faster if they breach licence conditions.

‌



Justice Secretary Alex Norris said: “Dangerous offenders should be under no illusion – if they break the rules we will know about it and put them behind bars.

Clacton by-election result as Nigel Farage beats Count Binface but refuses to attend READ MORE :

Families of road crash victims share harrowing failures as damning report demands change READ MORE :

View 2 Images Justice Minister Alex Norris said it is the biggest expansion of electrionic tagging in British history (Image: ITV)

“That’s why I’m launching the biggest expansion of tagging in British history, putting more criminals than ever under constant surveillance.

‌



“And we’re backing our probation officers with new tech to act fast when offenders step out of line. That means tough punishment in the community, victims put front and centre and a probation service focused on what matters most – keeping the public safe.”

Up to this point probation staff have had to request location information from the electronic monitoring provider. The new system means officers can access pinpoint location data within minutes.

It is already in place in London and is set to be rolled out nationally by the end of the year, the Ministry of Justice said. And former prisoners will also be sent notifications on their phones if they are close to an area they are not allowed to go to - warning them to turn back.

‌



Senior probation officer Amy Hughes said: “This is a real game changer for us. Previously, if we needed to check where someone had been, getting that information could take time. Now we can get a much clearer picture of their movements quickly and easily.

“It makes the day-to-day job simpler, but more importantly it gives you greater confidence that you can spot when something isn’t right. If someone’s behaviour is changing or their risk looks like it might be escalating, having that information at your fingertips helps you join the dots much sooner and take action before things potentially become more serious.”

The government is currently recruiting an additional 1,300 probation officers, on top of 2,300 brought into the service over the past two years.

‌



It comes after a backlash over measures that will see around 5,000 prisoners released early from next month. Labour passed legislation to ease the prison crisis after years of Tory failure - which saw a shortage of spaces mean there were less than 100 places to send criminals to in summer 2024.

Mr Burnham ordered a review when he became PM, and announced that sex offenders and child groomers - who had been set to be included in the early release scheme - would no longer qualify.

He has said he wants to go further following an outcry over the expected release of two of PC Andrew Harper's killers. The Prime Minister has ordered Mr Norris to draw up water-tight measures to keep them behind bars by the time Parliament returns at the start of September.

Article continues below

Currently those guilty of manslaughter are still eligible for early release.

Under the Sentencing Act, which became law earlier this year, prisoners serving time for some violent or sexual offences were set to become eligible for release halfway through their sentences, rather than serving the current tariff of two-thirds.

Criminals including burglars and thieves are among prisoners who will be considered for release a third of the way through their sentences, down from the current 40%.

News.title: Twelve dead in Hungary tourist bus crash after driver 'fell asleep at the wheel'
News.content:
Twelve dead in Hungary tourist bus crash after driver 'fell asleep at the wheel'

A tourist bus has crashed in Hungary killing 12 people and injuring dozens more with the vehicle having veered off a motorway and into a ditch

View 2 Images A bus has overturned killing 12 people (Image: ZOLTAN MATHE/EPA/Shutterstock)

Twelve people have been killed and dozens more are injured after a tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary with police saying it was likely the driver fell asleep.

The Polish bus was travelling eastbound near the town of Mezokeresztes when it overturned on the M3 motorway around 87 miles east of Hungary’s capital, Budapest, at around 1am on Sunday.

Emergency services tried to lift the rear axle of the 24-tonne bus to remove passengers trapped underneath before cranes arrived to move the whole vehicle, according to local reports.

In a statement, police said it was likely that the driver had fallen asleep at the wheel, causing the accident, and that he had been taken into custody.

View 2 Images Emergency services at the scene following the crash (Image: Zoltan Mathe/MTI via AP)

Army called in to help tackle wildfires as dozens of homes and acres of land destroyed across tinderbox Britain READ MORE :

Hungary's disaster management service said at 3am that emergency services were able to rescue 35 people from the coach but there were others who were trapped underneath it.

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that at least 12 people had died in the accident. He offered his condolences to the families of the victims and thanked rescue workers who were dispatched to the scene.

He wrote: "12 people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured during the night, when a Polish coach overturned into a ditch on the M3 motorway."

There were 47 people travelling on the bus according to Hungarian Interior Minister Gábor Pósfai, with some of those people who had been rescued seriously injured.

A statement from him read: "In the bus accident overnight on the M3 motorway, a bus with Polish license plate overturned. The police and firefighters went to the scene, as well as civilian assistance arrived to move the injured vehicle.

"According to current information in the accident, 12 people were killed. There were 47 people travelling on the bus, some of them were seriously injured. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims and thank you for the work of those involved in the rescue. The driver of the vehicle who suffered the accident has been taken into custody."

Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski wrote in a post on X that a "tragic bus accident involving Polish tourists" had occurred in Hungary and that his ministry was in contact with Hungarian authorities.

Article continues below

Polish President Karol Nawrocki expressed his "deep sorrow" over the accident. "I join the families and loved ones of the victims in prayer and deep sympathy," he wrote in a post on X.

News.title: People who fled Stourbridge fires start to return home
News.content:
People who had to flee their houses during the devastating Stourbridge fires are starting to return home.

Many families are only just discovering the extent of damage to their homes as West Midlands Fire Service allowed some behind the cordon after three days.

Nineteen properties across five streets have been fully destroyed with another 18 severely damaged.

Aerial images of the scene appear to show some houses have remained entirely intact while those next to them have been burnt to the ground.

Residents of Brunswick Gate, Landsgate, Ounty John Lane, Quarry Park Road and Racecourse Lane were asked to gather to speak to fire chiefs one by one.

They then learned if it was safe to return or if their home needed significant repairs or had been lost entirely.

The blaze was one of several being tackled across England and Wales on Thursday, the hottest day of the year so far.

Phil Garrigan from the National Fire Chief's Council (NFCC) said on Saturday that 11 major fires in the past 48 hours and 43 new wildfires since Friday have left services under "incredible pressure".

News.title: Reform proposes £50bn welfare bill cut with changes to disability payments for millions
News.content:
Reform UK says it would aim to cut about Â£50bn from the benefits bill and scrap the disability payments system, Pip, if it comes in to government.

Robert Jenrick, the party's treasury spokesperson, said the plans, to be set out in full on Monday, would be the most comprehensive overhaul to the welfare system in a generation and affect nearly three million people.

In an article for the Sunday Telegraph, external he said the current system is "suicidal empathy" and "a strange perversion of compassion".

Labour said it was "fantasy economics, built on stripping support from disabled people", while the Conservatives called it a "half-baked policy" and another "attempt to distract from" questions about the Â£5m gift party leader Nigel Farage received.

Reform's plans include making companies pay for any employees off sick for the first two years. Businesses with more than five employees would have to take out insurance to cover the cost.

Reform says this is modelled on the Dutch system and would incentivise employers to make adaptions and encourage people back to work to reduce their insurance premiums.

The party says they would cut the National Insurance contributions (NICs) paid by employers to offset the cost of this measure, insisting the change would be cost neutral for businesses.

In a policy document to be published next week, which the BBC has seen an extract of, the party estimates 2.89 million people would have their disability payments' removed, or modified, under plans to abolish Personal Independent Payments (Pip) for working age people.

The party would also remove the extra health-related payments on Universal Credit.

A new system, called a Health Security Allowance, would replace both Pip and the Universal Credit health element but only the most "severe, enduring and high-risk cases" would receive cash support, the document says.

Other claimants would be supported through a council-run programme to cover what Reform said would be the "verifiable additional costs" as a result of their disability.

To boost available support for people out of work, the party says it would spend an extra Â£1.85bn a year on interventions such as cognitive behavioural therapy, physiotherapy, and employment support.

Reform also wants to reform children's benefits, and is promising to align the system for anxiety, depression and ADHD in young people with its changes to the adult system. But this would only apply to new claimants.

News.title: Ariana Grande leaves problems at home as her tour hits the UK
News.content:
It feels inconsiderate of Ariana Grande to bring a tour called Eternal Sunshine to the UK at the tail end of the year's fifth heatwave. Haven't we suffered enough already?

But the fans packed into London's O2 arena on Saturday night didn't seem to care about the heat and the sweat.

They came ready to dance. Thousands of them, dressed in cat ears, bridal gowns and elaborate floral headpieces.

They scream when she references rumours she's back together with her ex, Ricky Alvarez. And they bounce in unison when she plays colourful club anthems like Into You and Break Free.

It's the first time Grande has played in the UK since 2019, partly because of Covid, but also because of her Oscar-nominated role in the movie musical Wicked.

She rewards fans with a few of Glinda's signature hair tosses, external and, more importantly, a two-hour show that highlights the incredible agility of the star's voice.

Sure, the production has all the paraphernalia a major pop tour - big sets, plumes of smoke, inspired choreography - but there are long stretches where it's just Grande on stage with her band. Her stunning, four octave vocals come first. Everything else is a distant second. And rightly so.

If you dig around on Grande's YouTube channel, there's a famous video of her recording the song Positions, external, directing her sound engineers as she layers vocal harmonies and ad libs, finding new note combinations on the fly.

It's a bravura performance that showcases her facility with melody and arrangement - and she essentially recreates it live on stage at the O2.

After the opening run of songs, she hushes the audience and spends two minutes looping her voice. First the lyric, "I don't care what people say, it's true", in high and low registers. Then she adds short phrases: "Won't break. Can't Shake. Deep breathsâ¦. Tight chest. Life. Death. Rewind."

They become the backbone of the next song, Eternal Sunshine.

They're also the backstory of the whole show.

News.title: Hunt wins third gold as Asher-Smith makes history
News.content:
Amy Hunt won her third gold medal of a potential historic quadruple and Dina Asher-Smith earned a spot in the record books as Great Britain's 4x100m relay stars put on a show at the European Championships.

Britain's new sprint sensation Hunt celebrated her third title in six days, following triumphs in the 100m and 200m, as the GB women's quartet claimed the hosts' second gold medal in a spectacular ending to Saturday's action in Birmingham.

The 24-year-old, who described her team-mates as "superwomen" and a "privilege to race with", will now attempt to become the first athlete to win four gold medals at a single edition in the event's 92-year history when the mixed 4x100m relay takes place on Sunday (approx 20:35 BST).

Team-mate Asher-Smith, meanwhile, achieved her seventh gold at the championships - 10 years after capturing her first.

With that, the 30-year-old matched the record tally also held by Norwayâs Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Croatian discus thrower Sandra Elkasevic.

Following her 200m bronze on Thursday, Asher-Smith also equalled Polish sprinter Irena Szewinska's overall record tally of 10 medals at the championships.

In an utterly dominant performance, Imani-Lara Lansiquot completed the job for a GB team which also featured 21-year-old student midwife Success Eduan, crossing the line in 42.05 seconds - more than a second clear of fellow medallists Switzerland (43.12) and Poland (43.15).

Hunt told BBC Sport: "I am stood next to the real life GOAT [greatest of all time]. She [Asher-Smith] is the most decorated European athlete in history.

"I am stood next to some amazing women. This girl [Eduan] is a midwife, she brings babies into the world. This girl [Lansiquot] wrote a play. We're all amazing.

"That was stunning to come together. I had the time of my life."

News.title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?
News.content:
Jason didn't want a "Coke can" â that's the nickname for a penis that has been enlarged with so much filler it resembles a stubby drink can.

"Some people go really overboard," Jason tells me when we meet in Manchester.

His procedure increased the girth of his penis by 16% - an amount he, and his partner, are really happy with. He says it has given him a "self-confidence boost".

"Everything still functions" as normal, Jason explains - just with "that extra little bit of width".

It is not clear how many men like Jason are having penis fillers. And you can't walk down the street and get a sense of it in the way you can visibly see the popularity of lip fillers. There is little regulation and there are no official records as anybody can start offering the procedure.

Penis fillers even became the topic of a bizarre conspiracy theory at the last Winter Olympics. Male ski jumpers were rumoured to be using fillers to increase the surface area of their suits so they could jump further.

However, some men have ended up in A&E with a penis turning black and skin "sloughing off" after a botched procedure. And the British Association of Urological Surgeons has issued warnings to men having these procedures.

So why are men doing it and what are the risks?

News.title: Feeling nervous about university? Current students offer advice to freshers
News.content:
Journalism student Kieran Miller was worried about money, but he compared student bank accounts and chose one that gave him a free 16-25 Railcard, and signed up for student discount schemes.

Though it might be exciting to see your first maintenance loan payment hit your bank account in one big lump sum, Kieran, 19, says you need to remember it has to last until the next instalment.

With the help of his mum, Kieran, from Swansea, made a provisional budget before moving away, but warns that it's easy to get caught up in the student experience and spend more than you planned to.

"When you start uni and you're living away from your family and you've got this new sense of freedom it was also really difficult to stay strict financially because you want to make mates with people," he says. "Someone might invite you to go for food or to go for a drink - and you're like, 'I don't really want to say no because this is a chance to connect with someone.'"

As well as student loans, most universities offer a variety of scholarships and bursaries, and it's worth checking whether you're eligible.

News.title: The influencers getting bitten while chasing the perfect shark shot
News.content:
Incidents of sharks biting humans are incredibly rare, but at least three influencers have been bitten by the animals in less than a year. Scientists say they're increasingly concerned about the rise in social media videos showing people swimming too close to sharks, touching or even riding them.

"I'm seeing these videos every single week now and it's way more than it ever used to be," says shark scientist Kristian Parton, who also hosts the 'Shark Bytes' YouTube channel. "We're going to see people ending up in really serious incidents with sharks."

In July, a fishing influencer almost lost his leg after being attacked by a reef shark whilst spearfishing. In December, a Chinese content creator was bitten in the Maldives. Both incidents were caught on camera.

Researchers at the International Shark Attack File, which tracks human-shark interactions worldwide, have also told the BBC they've seen a marked increase in the past three years of people being bitten while trying to take footage with sharks.

A recent study of "swim with wildlife" expeditions, external found influencers and photographers were the most likely to ignore safety instructions.

In February last year, a tourist in the Caribbean had both hands bitten off while trying to get a photograph of a bull shark from the shallows, according to local authorities. Two months later, a snorkeller in Israel carrying a "selfie stick" was killed by sharks, reportedly while trying to get photographs.

The risk of being bitten by a shark remains extremely low: the number of unprovoked shark attacks worldwide has remained broadly stable for the past 30 years, at about 70 bites per year.

While Tayane Dalazen was bitten by a nurse shark - known as a more docile species - some influencers have been filmed touching tiger sharks and even great whites.

"We're talking about a true apex predator, a very large wild animal," says Parton. "You wouldn't walk into the Serengeti and try and put your hand on the face of a lion."

Sharks will often use defensive or "exploratory" bites when presented by an unwelcome human in their personal space, he adds.

Human interactions can also cause stress to the animals. Scientific studies have shown that approaching or touching a shark leads to high levels of hormones called glucocorticoids. These can lead to a weakened immune system, increased mortality and aborted offspring.

"If you're approaching the shark and stressing it out, whether it be in a nursery habitat, a breeding ground, or a feeding area, you're depriving that shark of an area that's important to it to survive," explains Parton, "and that's definitely a problem."

One of the best-known shark content creators is Ocean Ramsey, a 38-year-old former model who shot to fame in 2019 after she was pictured swimming with one of the largest great white sharks ever seen.

News.title: I survived two years as prime minister in a hit new game - then my cabinet deserted me
News.content:
In No 10: Full Confidence, external, players who take on the precarious position of prime minister must balance the moods of four factions - their cabinet, backbenchers, the media, and the public - to remain in the game. Decisions are made across more than 300 fictional political scenarios, handwritten by Brewis.

The storylines range from the mundane - dealing with GP appointment waiting times - to the absurd.

"I have a two or three-part storyline where a dog is let loose into the House of Lords by a lobbyist during a vet bill and that spirals out of control," Brewis said.

Each scenario asks players to pick one action from three choices on the screen, with each potentially upsetting or pleasing the different factions.

Much like in real life, if one side completely turns against you your political career is finished.

While some situations may sound farcical, Brewis said he had plenty of real life examples to draw on as inspiration.

"I'd remember that MP who had a spider that he'd threaten MPs with, or when Boris Johnson walked into a fridge. I'm frantically writing them all down."

News.title: Athletics medal ceremonies postponed after fraud arrest
News.content:
Medal ceremonies at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were postponed after a man was arrested on suspicion of fraud.

Transport at the Alexander Stadium tournament was also suspended on Saturday as a result of the arrest and necessary security procedures.

Members of the crowd reported being held outside by security staff for more than an hour after the event finished, with a large police presence at the scene.

The evening session concluded with Great Britain winning a pair of gold medals in the men's and women's 4x100m relays.

Tournament organisers said transport was suspended while the necessary security measures took place, but operations had returned to normal in the early hours of Sunday.

A statement from Birmingham 2026 said: "The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships' family will always be our first priority.

"We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening."

More information relating to the postponed medal ceremonies is due to be released later.

A West Midlands Police spokesperson confirmed that a man in his 30s remains in custody for questioning.

The crowd at the Alexander Stadium appeared to be near its 23,000 capacity.

At one point during the session, there was an announcement that the six medal ceremonies, scheduled to take place after the final event between 22:00 and 23:00 BST were cancelled, understood to be in relation to the police incident.

People posted on social media, reporting "crazy queues" for the shuttle bus and blue flashing lights on the main road outside the stadium.

A statement on the event's official account, posted on X at 23:03, said: "We apologise for the significant delays in leaving the Alexander Stadium venue this evening.

"Buses and coaches will start to arrive and departures will begin to gradually take place.

"We thank you for your patience with this matter. Please listen to the instructions from the safety personnel and marshals who are there to support you."

News.title: Britain's youngest Formula E driver says talent isn't enough anymore
News.content:
Making split-second decisions while driving up to 200mph probably seems like a crazy task for most of us.

But Britain's youngest Formula E driver is learning to take it in his stride as his second season in the series draws to a close.

Back in 2024, Taylor Barnard became the youngest person to start an E-Prix and since then he's broken several other records - including becoming the youngest driver to secure a podium, pole and points in the sport.

So what's the 22-year-old got his sights set on now? The ultimate title, of course, world champion.

Barnard tells BBC Newsbeat he feels he got into racing by the "skin of my teeth", due to the extreme costs it takes to climb the motorsport ladder.

The immense financial backing needed to become a professional driver has been long known, with stars like Sir Lewis Hamilton speaking openly about the sacrifices his family made to get him a seat in Formula 1.

And Barnard feels if he was trying to climb the ranks now, he wouldn't make it due to prices being "so blown out of proportion".

News.title: Unauthorised sites are growing but travellers say they are forced to break the law
News.content:
The number of unauthorised Gypsy and traveller sites is on the rise, with developments often carried out over Bank Holiday weekends.

Since April, sites in Hertfordshire, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Bedfordshire and elsewhere have been transformed, prompting legal battles and local dismay.

In January, the number of unauthorised traveller caravans â those without planning permission â across England stood at 4,950, a 73% increase on January 2020's figure of 2,860.

The summer count also shows a rise, of 44% between July 2019 and July 2025, from 3,113 to 4,471.

A senior councillor in one affected area warns there has been a "loss of control" of the planning system, while villagers living near one site likened its rapid construction to a "military operation".

The government says unauthorised development is "totally unacceptable" and that councils have "strong powers" to tackle it.

But Cliff Codona, who founded and chairs the National Travellers' Action Group, says the planning system is like a "big dagger in their back" for travellers, leaving them no option but to "break the law".

So what do travellers say is driving some to act unlawfully, and what do others think?

News.title: Parents 'watering down baby milk' over high costs
News.content:
A baby bank says parents are turning to "unsafe" practices such as watering down baby formula milk to save money.

Megan Sinden, founder of Moorside Baby Bank in Consett, County Durham, said a couple of families spoke of putting less powder in to get another week's worth out of it, "which to me is quite dangerous".

She called for a cap on rising costs of formula, saying: "It's not a luxury item, it's a basic need for a baby."

Charity National Childbirth Trust (NCT) said its recent study found nearly half of parents (48%) were struggling more financially after having a baby, and added infant formula should always be prepared according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Infant formula is designed to provide the correct balance of nutrients for babies when mothers cannot or choose not to breastfeed, and adding extra water alters that balance.

The lower concentration can cause nutrient deficiency, coupled with the reduced ability of the baby's body to absorb the nutrients, NCT said.

"In turn, this can lead to poor weight gain, growth problems, and developmental delays," the spokesperson said.

"In serious cases, too much water in the formula may lead to more immediate health problems because a baby's body is not able to safely process the excess water."

The latest report, external by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) found the average retail price of some infant formula had increased by more than 25% in recent years.

Moorside Baby Bank opened in February 2025 and has so far helped 226 families with goods like clothes, nappies and baby wipes, which were mainly donated by the community.

Sinden, who is a community worker from nearby Stanley, said the bank struggled to get donations of baby milk "because it is so expensive" and instead relied on grants to buy the formula in.

News.content:
A number of people have died and four people have been taken to hospital following a two-vehicle crash in County Kildare.

The collision occurred on on the M9 Northbound at Junction 3 at about 03:00 local time on Sunday.

GardaÃ­ (Irish police) said a vehicle had been travelling on the wrong side of the carriageway when a head on collision occurred with a second car. They said there were a "number of fatalities".

The driver and front passenger, both female and aged in their 30s, of the second car have been removed from the scene to Tallaght University Hospital and both remain in critical condition.

A female rear seat passenger, aged in her 20s, was taken to St. Luke's General Hospital and is in a serious condition.

The third passenger, who is a child, has been removed to Children's Health Ireland at Crumlin and is in a serious condition.

The section of the M9 from Junction 3 to Junction 4 northbound and southbound remains closed with local diversions in place.

GardaÃ­ said FiosrÃº (the Office of the Police Ombudsman) has been notified of the incident.

FiosrÃº's on-call team of investigators attended the scene and an independent investigation is ongoing.

The watchdog said a FiosrÃº investigation relates to incidents involving contact with gardaÃ­ where a member of the public has died or been seriously injured.

It said a referral does not necessarily mean a garda or gardaÃ­ have been accused of wrongdoing.

News.title: Man with dementia given days to leave Sweden
News.content:
Torossian said the situation had been "awful" and "traumatic" for the family.

"I'm just worried that if the police go in and try and take him, how is that going to affect my dad. We just want him to have some dignity," she said.

"We want him to be treated like someone - he's very vulnerable, and I just feel that this is really ruthless and harsh."

Torossian said doctors had advised the Swedish authorities the process of moving Mason to the UK would pose a "danger to his life".

When the UK left the European Union (EU) on 31 January 2020, British citizens stopped being EU citizens, which meant they could no longer stay in Sweden with right of residence status.

During a transitional period, British citizens could apply for residence status under a withdrawal agreement between the UK and the EU - which ended on 31 December 2021.

Torossian explained due to Mason's health conditions, a 'god man' - a legally appointed trustee - was given power of attorney to look after her dad's affairs.

Documents from the Swedish Migration Agency, seen by the BBC, state an application for permanent residency for Mason was made on 21 December 2021.

However, it was refused on the grounds documents showing he met the grounds for residency were not submitted.

News.title: Attempted murder arrest at Surrey asylum hotel
News.content:
Police have arrested a man on suspicion of attempted murder at a hotel used to house asylum seekers.

Officers were called to reports of a stabbing at Stanwell Hotel in Staines, near Heathrow Airport, at 18:30 BST on Saturday.

One man in his 30s was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries, Surrey Police said.

A Somali national in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and remains in police custody, the force added.

"Due to the nature of the report, armed officers were dispatched to the scene and assisted with the arrest," Det Supt Kate Hyder said.

"There remains a police presence in the area while we carry out initial inquiries."

She added: "We understand this incident has caused concern within the local community, and I encourage you to speak to local officers."

Police said they were not looking for anyone else linked to the incident.

News.title: Nan grabbed dog and budgie and fled bungalow fire
News.content:
An 84-year-old woman grabbed her pet dog and budgie before leaving her much-loved home as it became gutted by fire, her granddaughter said.

Paula Fenton's bungalow in Willenhall, West Midlands, was among several homes damaged when a fire spread through gardens in the street, as firefighters tackled multiple fires in the region on Thursday.

Jade Fenton, 32, said her nan lost her home and nearly all her belongings, including hearing aids, jewellery, a wedding ring and other memories of her late husband.

"There's nothing left of it," said Jade. "She left in her slippers and pyjamas."

Three bungalows in Stonehouse Avenue were severely damaged, with two, including Paula's home, losing their roofs completely.

Fires, including one in Stourbridge where 19 homes were destroyed, prompted a government warning to millions of phones on Friday.

People were warned not to light anything that could spark a wildfire during the drought and heatwave conditions. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described the country as like "a tinderbox".
