Sports.title: Former Swansea City ballboy who was KICKED by Chelsea legend Eden Hazard set to sell vodka empire for £500million
Sports.content:
Former Swansea City ballboy who was KICKED by Chelsea legend Eden Hazard set to sell vodka empire for £500million

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A former Swansea City ballboy who was once kicked by Eden Hazard is set to sell his vodka empire for £500million, 13 years on from the infamous incident.

Charlie Morgan made headlines back in 2013 when he caused Blues icon Hazard to be sent off in a League Cup game. He had received the ball, dived on it – seemingly to waste time – and Hazard ended up kicking him to try and get the ball back.

The Belgian was given his marching orders, with football fans worldwide split over the ordeal between the attacking great and a teenager.

Now 30, though, Morgan has set himself up for life with vodka brand Au Vodka, which he created with school friend Jackson Quinn in 2015.

Now, according to Sky, Morgan and Quinn are in talks over a possible £500m sale to American drinks giant the Sazerac Company.

The duo have moved the business into very glitzy, 'fully gold' offices in their home city over the last few years, but may not have to work again if the sale goes through.

Former Swansea ballboy Charlie Morgan (left) - once kicked by Eden Hazard (right) - is set to sell his vodka empire for £500million

Morgan made headlines in 2013 when he dived on the ball as a ballboy and was kicked by the Chelsea forward

Au Vodka, which sells more than 35,000 bottles of the premium spirit per day, is currently headquartered in premises which not only feature a gold exterior but also boast a gold ceiling, gold café and gold signage – to match its signature gold bottles.

Announcing the move on LinkedIn, Charlie reflected on the brand's growth, proudly writing: 'Introducing….. The new Au Vodka HQ.

'We spent four years in our first office which was only 250 sq ft and only just fit myself, Jackson Quinn and Jordan Major (who was just 16 and packing orders!).

'We spent 5 years in a industrial unit in Swansea, where we grew the business exponentially and the team to 96 people, which we added a new mezzanine floor to house more people four times.

'Today we’ve moved into our new home - A fully gold HQ which really represents Au and what we stand for.'

Celebrities including Brazilian footballing legend Ronaldinho and former American boxer Floyd Mayweather are amongst those who have thrown their weight behind the brand, while fans have congratulated Charlie on the new headquarters, with one praising the business leader for staying 'true' by not moving out of Swansea.

Reports suggest negotiations have been going on for several months and an agreement is close.

Sazerac is understood to be keen to build their presence in Britain, with each founder reportedly set to take £100m each from any sale. They could yet retain roles in the company, too.

Hazard saw red for the incident, before the duo reunited in laughter years later

Sazerac are working with law firm Forsey, Au Vodka is represented by DLA Piper.

Even Hazard appears to be a fan after the pair reunited two years ago in a PR campaign that gripped the footballing world's interest.

The two men put their fraught history behind them, appearing together in a photoshoot to promote Charlie's vodka.

Hazard posted several photos on his social media accounts, posing with Morgan while holding a glass of blue raspberry Au Vodka.

He wrote on X: 'A nice thing about retirement is catching up with old friends. You have come a long way in 11 years my friend @charliem0rgan, @auvodka x @hazardeden10.'

Hazard shared several other pictures to his page, showing the two looking at a chess board that had a number of bottles of AU Vodka on it.

Sports.title: Arsenal vs Man City combined XI: Stats boffins give Enzo Maresca's side the edge heading into Cardiff clash and only ONE Gunners defender makes the cut
Sports.content:
Arsenal vs Man City combined XI: Stats boffins give Enzo Maresca's side the edge heading into Cardiff clash and only ONE Gunners defender makes the cut

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The new season is fast approaching and the biggest teams in England are readying themselves to battle it out for one of the world's most prestigious league prizes.

It has been all change over the summer, with the transfer window seeing prices skyrocket as fresh faces, both on the pitch and in the dugout, have joined the top flight.

Who will lift the trophy come next summer remains to be seen, but all the early signs are pointing towards two clear favourites: Premier League champions Arsenal and Enzo Maresca's Manchester City.

With their first clash of the new campaign getting under way today in Cardiff, the stats gurus over at Sofascore have given the lowdown on both teams, building an ideal XI.

And it seems that City have just about edged Arsenal on player count, beating their rivals by six players to five in a 4-3-3 formation. Let's take a look and let us know if you agree in the comments...

Who will lift the trophy come next summer remains to be seen, but all the early signs are pointing towards two clear favourites: Premier League champions Arsenal and Man City

With their first clash of the new campaign getting under way today in Cardiff, the stats gurus over at Sofascore have given the lowdown on both teams, building an ideal combined XI

Goalkeeper: Gianluigi Donnarumma (Man City).

Sofascore rating: 7.02/10

Sofascore has opted to start the big Italian between the sticks.

It is fair to say that, despite some hairy moments, Donnarumma’s debut season in England was largely a success. Despite narrowly missing out on the title, the former Paris Saint-Germain No1 commanded a defence that managed to keep 15 clean sheets in the Premier League last season. The 6ft 5in giant produced some excellent individual performances, as well as a number of miraculous moments.

Many fans may prefer his opposite number and Premier League Golden Glove winner, David Raya. However, with the Community Shield and the subsequent beginning of the new season looming, both keepers will have the opportunity to better the other. Donnarumma will surely be desperate to remind people just how great he can be.

It is fair to say that, despite some hairy moments, Donnarumma’s debut season in England was largely a success

Right back: Matheus Nunes (City)

Sofascore rating: 6.95/10

From one obvious inclusion to a more surprising one, Nunes beats out Jurrien Timber to earn the right back spot.

Nunes was, of course, originally signed to play central midfield, but in classic Pep Guardiola fashion the former City boss moulded the Portuguese international into a quintessentially modern inverted wing back. Nunes' calmness on the ball and ability to progress possession suit his new role perfectly and offer new boss Enzo Maresca an interesting option on the right-hand side.

Nunes's contributions for City have, for years, been underappreciated and overshadowed by the brilliance of his predecessor, Kyle Walker, but the facts don’t lie. Nunes has consistently performed well above what many football fans expect of him, as shown by his Sofascore ratings, and if City beat Arsenal at the weekend, Nunes will lift his sixth trophy with the Sky Blues in three years. He has already secured a Premier League title, an FA Cup, a Carabao Cup and a FIFA Club World Cup.

Nunes’ contributions for City have, for years, been underappreciated and overshadowed by the brilliance of his predecessor, Kyle Walker

centre-back: Gabriel (Arsenal)

Sofascore rating, 7.27/10

Gabriel was one of, if not the best, in his position last season, and with the new campaign less than two weeks away, the Brazilian will be eager to retain that status.

Fans will be buzzing not only to see whether Gabriel maintains the level of form he managed last season, but also for the next instalment of the centre-back's heated rivalry with Erling Haaland. Their battles and bust-ups have been an entertaining aspect of City-Arsenal title deciders and cup finals over the past three years.

The Norwegian currently has the upper hand after netting a brace to knock Gabriel’s Brazil out of the World Cup, and Gabriel will undoubtedly be looking for revenge.

Gabriel was one of, if not the best, in his position last season, and with the new campaign less than two weeks away, the Brazilian will be eager to retain that status

centre-back: Marc Guehi (City)

Sofascore rating, 7.30/10

Joining Gabriel at the heart of the defence is City's ball-playing centre-back, Marc Guehi.

With William Saliba unable to play at the Principality, the Cobham graduate is a no-brainer for this XI. Since joining City from Crystal Palace in January this year, Guehi has been nothing short of exceptional. Embodying the modern centre-half, the England international boasts the technical ability of an attacking midfielder while also possessing the capacity for brutish yet efficient defensive work.

If City are to keep the Premier League champions at bay in Cardiff, Guehi will be at the epicentre of their resistance.

If City are to keep the Premier League champions at bay in Cardiff, Guehi will be at the epicentre of their resistance

Left back: Josko Gvardiol (City).

Sofascore rating: 6.99/10

The last member of a stellar combined defence is the versatile Croatian.

Often credited with being able to play anywhere across the backline, today Gvardiol will slot in on the left of our starting XI, a wholly deserved inclusion even considering the tibial fracture that saw him miss the second half of last season.

Since his return the 24-year-old has looked back to his best, performing well in City's latest pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid.

The new City boss, Enzo Maresca, is likely to deploy Gvardiol in a similar role to the one Guardiola assigned to him, one that depends on the full-back inverting and being equally comfortable both on and off the ball. Gvardiol has always managed to fulfil this role well, transforming himself from a traditional centre-back into a goal-scoring and assist-providing full-back over the past two seasons.

The last member of a stellar combined defence is the versatile Croatian, Josko Gvardiol

Central midfield: Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Sofascore rating, 7.46

Anchoring what is a truly world-class midfield is the man who epitomises elite consistency in the Premier League today. Declan Rice was thought to be overvalued by Arsenal when they paid more than £105million for the midfielder in 2023 but since then most would agree that fee now looks like a bargain.

Over the past three seasons, Rice has only improved, with each game showcasing his acute defensive acumen while also yielding a respectable number of goals and assists, especially in big matches. Now, after bringing the Emirates faithful that elusive Premier League title, he will be aiming to add more silverware to the cabinet. The Gunners' skipper will have the opportunity to win his second Community Shield and Arsenal's 18th today.

Anchoring what is a truly world-class midfield is the man who epitomises elite consistency in the Premier League today: Declan Rice

Central midfield: Elliot Anderson (City)

Sofascore rating: 7.34/10

Joining Rice in midfield, just as he did for England in the summer, is City's big-money signing, Elliot Anderson.

£115million from a Nottingham Forest side that spent most of last year in a relegation battle seems like a steep price. However, I think it is safe to assume that Enzo Maresca and the City fans would have paid whatever was required for Anderson's services.

A player with the young man's qualities is like gold dust to the modern manager. His press resistance, combined with surgical passing and shooting, results in a truly devastating midfield profile.

If selected this weekend, it will be Anderson's competitive City debut, and he will be thrown in at the deep end against that Arsenal midfield. However, one might suggest that the champions will have more on their hands in the midfield battle with the new boy pulling the strings.

If selected this weekend, it will be Anderson's competitive City debut, and he will be thrown in at the deep end against that Arsenal midfield

Central midfield: Bruno Guimaraes (Arsenal)

Sofascore rating: 7.45/10

Speaking of big-money moves, rounding out the midfield three is the new £75million man, Bruno Guimaraes.

After a summer-long transfer saga, Mikel Arteta has finally got his man. The former Newcastle skipper completes a truly frightening Arsenal midfield that, with both quality and depth, is poised to begin the defence of its title.

All Premier League fans will be aware of Bruno's ability by now, so it will be fascinating to see how Arteta deploys the Brazilian and how he works alongside Declan Rice in the middle of the park, especially considering their similarities.

The former Newcastle skipper completes a truly frightening Arsenal midfield that, with both quality and depth, is poised to begin the defence of its title

Right wing: Bukayo Saka (Arsenal)

Sofascore rating, 7.24

Beginning our star-studded attack is the Starboy, Bukayo Saka.

The England third-place play-off hero is the latest Premier League player to fall somewhat victim to his own brilliance. His level of consistency over the past four seasons has given fans unrealistic expectations of the winger, yet he still meets them.

Any suggestion that Saka may take his foot off the gas after finally winning the title was ignored instantly after his performances at the World Cup, in which Saka showed that he is just getting started at the top level.

Saka's level of consistency over the past four seasons has given fans unrealistic expectations of the winger, yet he still meets them

Striker: Erling Haaland (City)

Sofascore rating: 7.31

Perhaps the most obvious selection: up top is the immutably excellent Erling Haaland.

Fresh off carrying Norway to their first-ever World Cup quarter-final, the big man will want to set the tone for the club season with a win against Arsenal, especially considering his and the champions' recent history. The Norwegian has a stellar record against the Gunners, scoring five goals and registering two assists in the nine matches he has played against them while at City.

Today's game will also be our first opportunity to see how Maresca will work utilise Haaland. The new boss has already explained that he is not going to be a copy-and-paste version of Guardiola's, so his decisions on Sunday will be of great interest to the tactical boffins.

Maresca has not historically set his teams up in a system that funnels the ball to one player, but he may have to adapt, much like his predecessor, to maximise Haaland's output.

The Norwegian has a stellar record against the Gunners, scoring five goals and registering two assists in the nine matches he has played against them while at City

Left wing: Christos Tzolis (Arsenal)

Sofascore rating: 7.71

The final member of the attack is another new Arsenal incoming, Greek international Christos Tzolis.

While Arsenal fans will know what to expect from Guimaraes, they could be forgiven for being less clued up on their new winger. They may be surprised to learn that Tzolis spent three years at Carrow Road with Norwich City and was even relegated with the Canaries in 2022. However, since then, the quick and direct winger has spent two years at Club Brugge, where he has really come into his own, winning three trophies in two seasons in Belgium alongside a Pro League Player of the Year award last season.

With the highest Sofascore rating in this whole XI, Arsenal fans should expect great things from the new boy, and Nunes should expect a serious headache.

Sports.title: Novak Djokovic hints at mystery health concern as tennis star, 39, suffers in Cincinnati humidity in shock defeat by rank outsider Thiago Agustin Tirante
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic hints at mystery health concern as tennis star, 39, suffers in Cincinnati humidity in shock defeat by rank outsider Thiago Agustin Tirante

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Novak Djokovic revealed he is battling a 'condition' after falling to his knees in apparent struggle during his shock defeat by Thiago Agustin Tirante.

The tennis great lost 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Saturday in a match that took two hours, 44 minutes in hot and humid conditions at the Cincinnati Open, and sparked concerns after the game.

'It's just a condition that I have, health-wise, that has been bothering me for the past couple of years,' Djokovic said after being questioned on his health. 'A lot of issues, especially when it is humid and it is hot.

'I did anticipate it (would be humid), but there are all these things, like nerves and everything involved that make it worse, and that's what happened.'

Djokovic, 39, appeared to struggle physically in the heat and had his 10-match winning streak in Cincinnati snapped.

He has had plenty of success in Cincinnati, with a 45-13 record and titles in 2018, 2020 and 2023. But he wasn't sure he would return.

Novak Djokovic falls to his knees during his R2 match in Cincinnati.



During the changeover, Novak appeared to be vomiting before receiving a medical timeout. #cincytennis pic.twitter.com/hHwxVQY5BB — Tennis Channel (@TennisChannel) August 15, 2026

Novak Djokovic hinted at an unknown health condition follow his defeat at the Cincinnati Open

The tennis great admitted he is unsure if he will ever return to the tournament after the loss

'I certainly hope so, but it looks more likely not, unfortunately,' Djokovic said. 'But let's see what the future brings.'

A 25-year-old from Argentina, Tirante is ranked No50 in the world. Djokovic – a three-time Cincinnati champion and No5 in the rankings – was playing for the first time since his loss to top-ranked Jannik Sinner in the semifinals at Wimbledon.

Up next for Djokovic is the US Open, which starts August 30 in New York.

Djokovic saved 13 of the 15 break points he faced. Tirante broke Djokovic's serve in the ninth game of the final set and then served it out.

'I think this is the best win of my career,' Tirante said. 'I think I really did a good job inside the court. I managed very well the nerves of playing against a legend like Novak.'

In a rain-delayed match that ended at 2.15am Sunday, top-seeded Alexander Zverev rallied to avoid a third straight loss, beating Cameron Norrie 3-6, 6-3, 6-3. After losing to Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon final, Zverev – the French Open champion – returned to play in Montreal and fell to Tallon Griekspoor in his opener Aug. 5.

On the women's side, Alexandra Eala of the Philippines continued her run of strong play with a victory over Elena-Gabriela Ruse, who lost the first set and stopped playing in the second with an ankle injury. Eala – who is No20 in the rankings - won her first WTA singles title in Washington earlier this month and has won eight of her last nine matches.

American Jessica Pegula beat Simona Waltert 6-3, 6-2, improving her record to 25-6 on hard courts in 2026. The third-ranked Pegula won the title in Cincinnati in 2024.

Sports.title: West Brom star sparks controversy with handball goal in Championship opening day win - leaving opposing manager livid
Sports.content:
West Brom star sparks controversy with handball goal in Championship opening day win - leaving opposing manager livid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Brom star Aune Heggebo left fans stunned as he scored with his hand on the opening day – with officials missing the offence.

The Baggies were well below par in their 2-1 victory over Norwich at Carrow Road on Saturday afternoon, but managed to claim victory following strikes from Heggebo and new signing Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

It was a far from routine win for James Morrison's side, and the main takeaway from the game was Heggebo's opening goal, which clearly came off his arm.

The Norway forward raced in to tap home Morgan's cross, but, as he raised his leg to try and poke it in, he raised his arms too.

The ball struck his left arm and fell into the net, with Norwich players protesting to referee Tim Robinson – who missed the incident.

Heggebo wheeled away in celebration, with none of the officials noticing he had in fact committed an offence to score.

Aune Heggebø’s goal for West Bromwich Albion against Norwich City has fuelled controversy over an alleged handball.



Should the goal have stood? 💭 pic.twitter.com/TcKQ4ctV9N — ITV Football (@itvfootball) August 15, 2026

West Brom star Aune Heggebo stunned fans with a handball goal on the opening day of the Championship season

'It was clearly with the arm that the player scores – we could see that from where we were watching, 50 yards away,' Norwich manager Philippe Clement said after the game. 'It was the decisive moment in the game and should have been spotted.

'There are four officials and one of them should have seen it. Maybe the referee didn't have the best view – but the linesman on our side needs to see that. Missing game-changing moments like this shouldn't happen – it has cost us at least two, maybe three points.'

Morgan, who joined for £4million from Chelsea this summer, added a second goal in the 87th minute, with Mathias Kvistgaarden's 90th minute goal proving to be nothing but a consolation.

Fans on social media were left stunned by the incident, with one writing: 'Cracking header from Heggebo tbf.'

Another wrote: 'You could see it on Aune Heggebo after the goal that he had cheated, and it's just unbelievable that neither the referee nor linesman sees this.

'I'll take one of these in every single match this season over VAR anyway.'

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala appears to FAINT while playing for Bayern Munich in extreme heat - as team-mate rushes over to catch Germany star
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich and Germany star Jamal Musiala appeared to pass out during his side's friendly win over RB Leipzig, sparking concern among players and fans.

The midfielder had just scored to make it 3-1 to his side in the 81st minute, but appeared dazed and confused just two minutes later before he was caught by new team-mate Ismael Saibari.

After the Morocco star lowered him to the ground, medical staff rushed onto the field as Bayern players surrounded the 23-year-old.

Amid a hush from the crowd, the medical staff eventually gave a thumbs up, with reports in Germany suggesting that Musiala had struggled with the 33 degrees Celsius heat.

Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer said after the game: 'It will become clear what it was. But of course we are keeping our fingers crossed.'

Director of sport Max Eberl, meanwhile, said: 'He is fine, and that is the most important thing.'

Jamal Musiala appeared to faint during Bayern Munich's pre-season friendly victory

New footage emerged after the incident to show Musiala looking uncomfortable just after scoring his goal, and two minutes later he had collapsed.

The incident comes following a debate around hydration breaks, which were held regularly during the World Cup.

Bayern, meanwhile, won the game 3-1, with Luis Diaz, Nathaniel Brown and Musiala on the scoresheet.

Musiala, who played at the World Cup with Germany, had only been introduced as a 69th minute substitute, but had to leave the field of play soon after.

England captain Harry Kane was not involved in the game but returned to training alongside the likes of Michael Olise this week.

Bayern kick off their competitive season next weekend in the German Super Cup, when they will take on Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: Babar Azam injury concerns, an awkward captaincy change and usual off-field maelstrom - Pakistan mirror England's chaos and Test series will be packed with drama
Sports.content:
New captain, interim coach, players recalled who had not previously featured in 2026. If England’s lot this summer befell Pakistan, it would be considered par for the course.

This coming week, with incoming Test coach Stephen Fleming not ready to take up his role, Joe Root and Marcus Trescothick will form a temporary leadership alliance, while Dan Lawrence, Ollie Pope and Sam Cook return to the fray in Leeds.

England are desperate to create some stability after reaching the end of the Bazball era with the midsummer departures of Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum, but if one team in world cricket is accustomed to dealing with the unsettling elements of wholesale change it is Pakistan.

Some will even argue that rather than run from chaos, they embrace it, and in keeping with dull moments being conspicuous by their absence where their cricket is involved, captain Babar Azam provided a pre-series scare on Friday when he was forced to retire hurt and pull out of the remainder of the warm-up match against a County Select XI.

Failing to ride a rising delivery from Hampshire’s teenage seamer Manny Lumsden, Babar was struck on the right glove and immediately began wringing his hand in discomfort.

Team insiders insist the removal was a precautionary measure and that although there was no sign of a fracture, the fact that it was the same middle finger Pakistan’s premier batsman damaged during the recent Test win over West Indies in Trinidad meant no chances were being taken.

Babar Azam, pictured earlier this year ahead of a Test against West Indies, gave his side an injury scare this week ahead of the England clash at Headingley

That eight-wicket victory earlier this month was Pakistan’s first overseas for three years, ending a sequence of eight straight defeats, and although Babar’s brief sidelining removed the chance to further develop the on-field bond between this latest combination of players, he is pencilled in to rejoin them in the nets at Headingley on Monday, 48 hours before the first Test of three begins.

Mirroring the situation England found themselves in, a level of awkwardness surrounded Pakistan’s most recent captaincy change ahead of the 1-1 series draw in the Caribbean.

The strong friendship between Joe Root and Harry Brook has diluted the issue from an English perspective after Stokes nominated the latter as his successor during his farewell at Trent Bridge, and Brook followed up with a public pitch to become captain across all formats.

Arguably, Pakistan had to overcome something slightly worse, though, with Shan Masood axed after three years in charge but retained in the XI under Babar. The response offered mixed results: although Masood scored a first-innings hundred, the match ended in defeat and him nursing a finger injury that would keep him out of the second match.

It was partly for his statesmanlike demeanour that Masood replaced Babar as captain in 2023 and it is for his diplomatic communication skills that former captain Rashid Latif suggested this week a novel relationship could now develop. Masood, he argued, should continue with media interactions, shielding Babar and allowing him to concentrate on directing operations in the middle now he has the armband back.

‘An England tour is a difficult assignment, and the English media often tries to unnecessarily involve visiting teams in news stories,’ he claimed.

To be fair, previous Pakistan teams touring here this century have provided plenty of material of their own. Think back to Inzamam-ul-Haq walking his team off the field and forfeiting The Oval Test amid ball tampering accusations from officials in 2006 or the spot-fixing scandal that grubbed the series four years later as examples.

But Latif’s desire for Babar to concentrate on lifting Pakistan’s Test cricket out of the doldrums is well meaning. Languishing in eighth in the current World Test Championship standings, one place below England, they have won just one of their previous eight series - against Stokes’ side in the autumn of 2024.

Shan Masood (left) was stripped of the captaincy but is still in the team under Azam (right)

And dealing with the off-field maelstrom in a cricket-mad country is never easy. Just this week, Shaheen Shah Afridi was batting away suggestions that Babar will be replacing him as Pakistan’s one-day captain imminently. There is also talk of Salman Ali Agha making way in Twenty20.

In Pakistani cricket circles, there is always someone ready to take your job. When Agha was appointed last year, he became his country’s fourth T20 captain in 14 months.

The same goes with coaches. Sarfaraz Ahmed leads this tour, but only after surviving calls for his head following the 2-0 defeat to Bangladesh. He only moved into the post in April.

Gary Kirsten, the man who guided India to the No 1 Test ranking and 2011 World Cup glory, lasted only six months in charge of Pakistan’s white-ball teams during 2024.

Jason Gillespie, their other high-profile foreign appointment in a split coaching set-up, didn’t stick around much longer.

Both were upset by external interference in team affairs, with Gillespie refusing to let success against England during the 2-1 home win two years ago cloud his judgment. He had been reduced to a ‘match-day analyst’, he said, adding that ‘it wasn’t what I signed up for.’

Whatever happens over the next month, those investing emotions in a series like this are unlikely to be disappointed by the drama that unfolds.

Past Pakistan dramas:

2001: England’s attempts to save a match at Old Trafford, and thereby win a fifth series in a row, were marred by Pakistan taking four wickets with no balls. The umpiring errors from David Shepherd and Ed Nichols, in the days before technology was used automatically to check bowlers overstepping, helped Pakistan to a win with less than seven overs remaining. Three of the officiating errors came at the legendary Shepherd’s end, with Saqlain Mushtaq the benefactor.

2006: Inzamam-ul-Haq became the first captain in 129 years to forfeit a Test match after taking umbrage at being punished for ball-tampering on the fourth day of the Oval Test. What began as a five-run penalty imposed by the umpires - Australian Darrell Hair and Billy Doctrove, of West Indies - soon escalated into a major diplomatic incident, with Pakistan refusing to take the field after tea, leading to Hair removing the bails and England being declared winners in the record books.

Inzamam-ul-Haq is pictured in 2006 - the Pakistan captain forfeited after a ball-tampering scandal

2010: The actions of three of Pakistan's best players - captain Salman Butt, along with bowlers Mohammad Amir and Mohammad Asif - shook the sporting world following a newspaper sting that showed them to be participating in a betting scam known as spot-fixing.

Amir’s brilliance had England on the ropes at 102 for seven before Jonathan Trott and Stuart Broad produced a Test record eighth-wicket stand of 332. Both their achievement, and England’s innings victory, were inevitably tarnished when it emerged no-balls had been delivered to order for cash. All three men were jailed and handed lengthy bans from cricket.

2016: Lord’s was a much happier place this time as veteran captain Misbah-ul-Haq led the tourists to a 75-run win remembered for his reaction to his 10th Test hundred. To mark the 154-ball effort, the 42-year-old dropped his bat and peeled off 10 press-ups, in tribute to the army officers who had put the Pakistan squad through their paces pre-tour. The fitness regime was acknowledged again by the entire squad post-match, with a group press-up celebration.

Sports.title: Named: The Premier League club whose fans will have to fork out nearly £5,000 to follow their team this season - as staggering new data reveals where every side ranks, with surprise No 1
Sports.content:
'Football without fans is nothing,' the great Celtic manager Jock Stein once said. Looking at the state of modern matchday prices, which are pricing out droves of loyal supporters, those words have rarely felt truer. New data has revealed that it could cost £5,000 to follow the most expensive team in the Premier League this season home and away - and that's a conservative estimate. The unlucky fanbase is that of Bournemouth, whose followers would have to shell out £4,911.61 to watch them home and away this coming campaign without a season ticket. That includes extortionate train costs, plus a pie and two pints at every game, and a replica kit. The second and third-most expensive are Sunderland and Newcastle - all three place so high because of their extreme geographies, meaning the travel costs rack up. By contrast, the cheapest club to follow would be Brentford with a season ticket, but that still comes to £2,827.26 when you price in travel, grub, and alcoholic fare. The costliest 'Big Six' team to follow is Arsenal, who are the fourth-most expensive club to watch with or without a season ticket. Bournemouth are the most expensive team to follow in the Premier League if you factor in ticket costs, travel prices, food and drink, and a jersey

Your browser does not support iframes.

Tracking the Gunners home and away would set you back £3,748.56 with a season ticket and £4,349.06 without - the sort of money Bukayo Saka earns in two-and-a-half hours. By comparison, the other 'Big Six teams' are quite cheap to follow. While Tottenham's ticket prices are second only to Arsenal, overall they are the ninth-most-dear team to follow thanks to London's national train connections. Meanwhile, Manchester United come in 12th, Liverpool are 14th, Chelsea rank 16th, and Manchester City place 17th, arguably showing a stronger value for money. Only Coventry, Leeds, and Brentford would be cheaper to follow as a whole package than City, who will set back fans £3,059.22 with a season ticket and £3,424.22 without. Alright, then, you ask, where can I fill my stomach the cheapest? The answer to that is Hull, where a pie costs a reasonable £3 - 20 pence cheaper than their nearest competitors in Hull City. Every other club will charge you over £4, most will hit you for more than £5, and Arsenal have the audacity to demand £8.85, according to last season's menu. Being one of Arsenal's victorious supporters comes at a price - they've got the costliest tickets in the Premier League If you're looking to wet your whistle with a couple of beers, it's Ipswich where you can do that on the cheap, for just £3.50. Coventry (£3.60) and Hull (£.90) are the next-cheapest, though they could raise their fares for the coming campaign. Arsenal are once again the culprits in this department, asking their supporters for £6.80 per pint, though most things do cost more in London generally. It wouldn't be right to follow your team home and away without a little bit of merchandise, so how about a replica men's shirt for the 2026-27 campaign? You're in luck, Hull faithful, as your kits come out the most affordable at £64. Ipswich, Brentford, and Crystal Palace trail closely on £65. Tottenham - whose performances in recent seasons few people would actually want to replicate - are the most expensive to imitate in the stands. They have the brass neck to ask for £90 for a replica kit, though Chelsea are hot on their heels at £89.99. Overall, the average cost of following your club with a season ticket, with trains, pints, pies, and a replica kit thrown in, costs £3,450.56 in the Premier League. Brentford are the cheapest team to follow, partly thanks to London's good transport links Doing so without a season ticket - which, in fairness, few people would do in totality - raises that financial sacrifice to £3,902.44. It is little wonder that we see regular protests against clubs' ticket prices, and similarly constant grumblings about the cost of rail travel in this country. Fans are gouged another £730 if they sign up to every broadcasting platform available in the United Kingdom to watch Premier League games - and that doesn't even give you access to every game. In Singapore, viewers are able to watch all 380 matches on Premier League + for a monthly payment of £25. Where would football be without the fans, eh?

Sports.title: Aston Villa in talks with Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki as PSG move crumbles, and West Ham break Championship transfer record for Arne Engels: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa plot swoop for Suzuki as PSG deal crumbles

Aston Villa have rekindled talks for Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuki after the collapse of his move to Paris Saint-Germain.

The Japan international was scheduled to have a medical with PSG today but the French club indicated the commission demanded by agents, was considered too high and the deal fell through.

Zion Suzuki has rekindled talks with Aston Villa after his Paris Saint-Germain move fell through

Villa have Emiliano Martinez as their number one who was expected to stay after the World Cup but had been a target for Juventus.

The Italians fell short in their initial offers for Martinez and have been discussing a loan for Guglielmo Vicario from Tottenham and Ederson at Fenerbahce.

Villa, meanwhile, are wrapping up the signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atletico Madrid, and Halmstad BK have expressed their interest in Villa striker Rory Wilson.

City close to Bouaddi deal

Manchester City are close to concluding talks for Lille’s £85million-rated midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi as Barcelona press to sign Rodri.

Bouaddi, the 18-year-old Morocco international, started on the bench for Lille in their friendly at Everton yesterday and coach Davide Ancelotti confirmed negotiations.

Lille have been fighting to keep the midfielder for one more season, but City and the player want to seal a move now, which is expected to come at a premium.

'Of course, there are negotiations,' admitted Ancelotti. 'There is interest from so many clubs. He is a really, really good player and I hope that he is going to stay with us!

'He is incredibly intelligent on and off the pitch, he is really mature. He is 18-years-old but he looks like he is 32 when he is on the pitch. He’s going to be one of the best midfielders in Europe for the next 10 years.'

The teenager's arrival at City would help offset the loss of Spain captain Rodri who is set in a move to Barcelona.

The Spanish champions have made a third proposal worth around £60m for the 30-year-old and hope that City agree on a compromise to sell.

City maintain an interest in midfielder Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea's Friday's deadline passing without the necessary £120m bid being made. Tottenham are also expected to make an offer for City winger Savinho.

Newcastle's talks progress with Benfica's Dedic

Newcastle are advancing in talks to sign Bosnia right-back Amar Dedic from Benfica.

Talks are continuing over a £30million fee for the 23-year-old and he is expected to arrive on Tyneside on Sunday.

The 23-year-old played under coach Matthias Jaissle at RB Salzburg.

Newcastle have also considered going back into the market for Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as they search for a midfielder.

Palhinha has interest from Aston Villa and Benfica but Bayern only want a permanent sale not a loan.

Newcastle are advancing in talks to sign Bosnia right-back Amar Dedic from Benfica

Spurs reach agreement with Boro for Phillips

Tottenham defender Ashley Phillips is ready to complete his protracted move to Middlesbrough.

The deal was held up last weekend after concerns over his medical. However, following further tests and discussions, the clubs have reached an agreement.

He is due on Teesside this weekend to finalise his switch to the Riverside.

Boro kick off their Championship campaign at home to Lincoln City today.

Tottenham defender Ashley Phillips is ready to complete his protracted move to Middlesbrough

Coventry bolster attack

Coventry City are in talks with Fenerbahce over a £21million deal for striker Sidiki Cherif.

As well as agreeing to sign Nottingham Forest's Taiwo Awoniyi, manager Frank Lampard wants Cherif who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January.

The 19-year-old scored three goals in 14 games for Fenerbahce.

Benfica offer for Harwood-Bellis rejected

Southampton have rejected a £17.5million offer from Benfica for defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Portuguese side, coached by Marco Silva, turned to the 24-year-old after initial interest in Chelsea's Tosin Adarabioyo who wants to stay at Stamford Bridge.

Benfica are considering an improved offer with Harwood-Bellis interested in the move.

Benfica are considering an improved offer for Saints' Harwood-Bellis after having their initial bid of £17.5million rejected, while the 24-year-old is interested in the move

Forest sign former Fulham goalkeeper Benda

Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of former Fulham goalkeeper Steven Benda.

The 27-year-old is being brought in to replace the departed Angus Gunn as third-choice. He had spells on loan at Feyenoord and Millwall last season.

Eagles sign £21m right back Khalaili

Crystal Palace have completed the £21million signing of Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili.

Khalaili's move to Inter Milan fell through earlier this summer over a health issue, but he passed his medical with Palace last weekend.

The 21-year-old is being brought in to provide competition for Daniel Munoz at right wing-back.

However, there is no guarantee that the £20m-rated Colombian will stay beyond this summer amid interest from the likes of Tottenham and Everton. He has two years left on his deal.

Khalaili, who has won 16 caps for Israel, said: 'I'm happy to be here, I'm excited, and I can't wait to start.

'I’ve followed the Premier League. It's a new challenge for me, and I've followed Crystal Palace for a long time. I'm happy to be here.'

Khalaili's move to Inter Milan fell through earlier this summer over a health issue, but he passed his medical with Palace last weekend

Gourna-Douath 'excited' to join Tigers

Hull City have finalised the £3.5m transfer of French defensive midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath from RB Salzburg.

The deal is worth £2.9m guaranteed, plus add-ons and a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

The 23-year-old has signed a five-year contract, becoming the club’s 10th summer signing.

Gourna-Douath said: 'I’m really happy because it was such a long journey from the first phone call until I signed. I’m so excited to get started.

'I’m really happy to have this experience. I got a chance to play in the Champions League, Serie A and Ligue 1.

'I've learned a lot and I’m really happy to put this experience on the pitch in the Premier League. The Premier League is the dream of all footballers. Now, I have a chance to play in the Premier League, so I am excited to play.'

Leeds agree £6.8m move for Eveldi

Leeds United have agreed a fee with Borussia Monchengladbach for Nico Elvedi.

The deal is understood to be worth an initial £6.8m plus add-ons.

The central defender was left out of Gladbach’s squad for today’s friendly against Aston Villa.

His arrival would open the door for Sebastiaan Bornauw to join Hamburg.

Gladbach have also negotiated a 15 per cent sell-on.

Black Cats ink Methalie deal

Sunderland have reached a full agreement with Toulouse to sign 20-year-old full-back Dayann Methalie.

The fee is understood to be £26million including add ons.

Methalie has agreed a five-year contract.

West Ham break Championship record for Engels

West Ham have signed Belgium international Arne Engels from Celtic for a Championship record £22 million.

Engels has joined West Ham on a five-year deal, as the East London side attempt to make an immediate return to the Premier League.

The versatile midfielder adds creativity to the Championship outfit and is renowned for his set-piece delivery.

He is not, however, eligible for their second-tier opener against Burnley tomorrow and will have to wait until next weekend’s home game against Charlton to make his debut.

Celtic have doubled their money on Engels, who they bought from German club Augsburg two years ago.

West Ham have broken the Championship transfer record with the signing of Arne Engels

Engels, capped four times by Belgium, said: ‘It's a really nice project to come into and try to go back to the Premier League. That's the big goal.

‘That’s everybody's goal and it's just up to me to hopefully help the team with it and, together with the supporters, to get some wins.

‘Hopefully, we'll see that it's going to be a good year then and I'm looking forward to the next ones.

‘I'm just looking forward to meeting all the fans at London Stadium. I’m looking forward to this challenging season, but hopefully we can make it a really good one, so let's go for it!’

And the best of the rest...

FOREST have signed former Fulham goalkeeper Steven Benda.

SUNDERLAND have reached agreement with TOULOUSE to sign 20-year-old full-back Dayann Methalie for £26m including add ons.

Méthalie has agreed a five-year contract.

LEEDS UNITED have agreed a £6.8m fee plus add ins with BORUSSIA MONCHENGLADBACH for Nico Elvedi. The deal opens the door for Sebastiaan Bornauw to join HAMBURG.

Gladbach have also negotiated a 15 per cent sell-on.

LIVERPOOL remain in positive talks for PARIS ST GERMAIN winger Bradley Barcola.

Southampton and SHEFFIELD UNITED are interested in FEYENOORD defender Anel Ahmedhodzic.

BRENTFORD have signed midfielder Darwin Guagua, 18, from Independiente del Valle and will loan him to Mérida.

UDINESE, CELTIC and HAMBURG are talking to BLACKBURN about goalkeeper Balazs Toth.

RANGERS have completed the loan signing of left-back James Penrice from AEK ATHENS.

HULL CITY have signed Joe Gelhardt from Leeds for £6.5m and finalised the £3.5m transfer of Lucas Gourna-Douath from RB Salzburg.

The deal is worth £2.9m guaranteed plus add-ons and a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

WATFORD forward Nestory Irankunda has completed his £17million move to SPORTING LISBON where he has signed a five-year deal and has a release clause of £68.5m.

CARDIFF have re-signed Calum Scanlon on loan from LIVERPOOL for the season.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool's Barcola boost, £60m for Arsenal to sign star, double Spurs deal
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola could be on his way to Liverpool

All of the latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and more

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer live blog for Sunday, August 16.

Liverpool have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola as a result of Paris Saint-Germain signing Mika Godts from Ajax. There was speculation that the Ligue 1 champions would be willing to trim their £145million valuation of the 23-year-old, but only if they secured a solid replacement on the left.

Having done so, it's now a waiting game to see whether the rumour mill has churned truth with regards to a potential cut-price deal for Barcola. The Frenchman has been a priority target for Liverpool for the majority of the summer, as Andoni Iraola looks for further firepower up the top end of the pitch to challenge in 2026/27.

Arsenal, meanwhile, may have to fork out at least £60m if they hope to sign Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen before next month's transfer deadline, according to sources speaking with Football Insider.

The Gunners are also looking for attacking threat this summer, having missed out on Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior following a long and drawn out transfer saga. They could now turn their attention to 27-year-old Osimhen, who has been linked with a move to the Premier League for the past couple of years, only for a deal to fail to come to fruition.

On the other side of North London, Tottenham Hotspur are eyeing moves for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo and Manchester City's Savinho, as a summer of massive spending continues. Reports from the Netherlands suggest that Gakpo has reached an agreement in principle with regards to personal terms, with a £70m price tag being touted for his transfer.

Savinho, meanwhile, has reportedly shared an interest in working under Roberto De Zerbi this season, with Spurs looking to wrap up an £85m move for the Brazilian.

At the Etihad Stadium, the Cityzens are on the brink of securing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in an £85m swoop of their own, as Rodri closes in on a move to Barcelona. Having already welcomed Elliot Anderson in a £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, City have now turned their attention to finding a suitable playing partner for the 23-year-old.

Bouaddi, 18, could be just that, following a formidable World Cup campaign with Morocco.

Stay tuned for all of the latest news and updates in our transfer blog below...

Sports.title: European Athletics Championships thrown into chaos after 'police incident' in Birmingham
Sports.content:
European Athletics Championships thrown into chaos after 'police incident' in Birmingham

Athletics fans trying to leave Alexander Stadium on Saturday night faced lengthy delays, with West Midlands Police later confirming that a man had been arrested on suspicion of fraud

View 2 Images Fans struggled to get out of Alexander Stadium on Saturday night (Image: Michael Steele/British Athletics via Getty Images)

Medal ceremonies at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were postponed on Saturday evening and transport was suspended after a man was arrested on suspicion of fraud.

‌



Tournament organisers said transport operations had returned to normal in the early hours of Sunday. A statement from Birmingham 2026 read: “Birmingham 2026 can confirm that transport operations have returned to normal following a police incident on Saturday evening.

‌



“Championship transport was suspended until the necessary security measures had been carried out whilst West Midlands Police arrested a man in his thirties on suspicion of fraud. The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships’ family will always be our first priority.

‌



“We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening. Further information will be issued on Sunday relating to the evening’s postponed medal ceremonies.”

A West Midlands Police spokesperson confirmed that a man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of fraud and remained in custody for questioning.

The crowd at the Alexander Stadium appeared to be near its 23,000 capacity to watch Saturday’s evening session, which concluded with Great Britain winning a pair of gold medals in the men’s and women’s 4x100m relays.

‌



At one point during the session, there was an announcement that the six medal ceremonies, scheduled to take place after the final event between 10pm and 11pm, were cancelled. The Press Association understands this decision was taken in relation to the police incident.

Outside, there was a visibly heavy police presence and huge static queues of people waiting for shuttle buses. Alex Ridout wrote on X: “Crazy queues for the shuttle bus after tonight’s European Athletics Championships session.

View 2 Images Britain won gold in the men's and women's 4 x 100 relay on Saturday night (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



“Definitely seems like something has gone on that has potentially caused blockages, with blue flashing lights seen on the main road outside Alexander Stadium.”

Another user, Paul, posted shortly after midnight: “We are one of the last out of the pens. Been queuing since 10.15 with 3 kids who all needed the toilet. In the stadium has been good but the planning on getting out has been abysmal. There was little communication from anyone about the issue!”

Susie Barnacle wrote on X that she had been “waiting for nearly two hours to leave” and described “armed police at the buses”, adding: “We were told precisely nothing!”

Article continues below

Several people on social media said they were told there had been a “security incident”. Michele wrote on X: “What’s happening at the Alexander Stadium? Police saying there’s a security incident and hundreds of people waiting for buses.”

A statement on the event’s official account, posted on X at 11:03pm, read: “We apologise for the significant delays in leaving the Alexander Stadium venue this evening. Buses and coaches will start to arrive and departures will begin to gradually take place.

“We thank you for your patience with this matter. Please listen to the instructions from the safety personnel and marshals who are there to support you.”

Sports.title: Ian Machado Garry confronts UFC rival just moments after Islam Makhachev loss
Sports.content:
Ian Machado Garry confronts UFC rival just moments after Islam Makhachev loss

Machado Garry nearly found himself involved in another clash just moments after going 25 minutes with welterweight champion Islam Makhachev

View Image Ian Machado Garry confronted UFC rival Michael Morales just moments after his loss to Islam Makhachev

Ian Machado Garry was involved in a rather tense backstage face-off with UFC rival Michael Morales just moments after his loss to Islam Makhachev.

‌



The Dublin scrapper fell short in his first shot at UFC gold on Saturday night at UFC 330. Machado Garry, 28, showed glimpses in the third round, but ultimately, Makhachev's championship experience paid dividends. The welterweight king would go on to get the nod on all three of the judges' scorecards.

‌



After going 25 minutes with the men's pound-for-pound number one, Machado Garry was almost involved in another dust-up just minutes later. As the 28-year-old made his way backstage, the Irishman bumped into fellow welterweight star Morales. Several words were exchanged before the pair eventually shook hands and parted ways.

‌



"All the s*** you talk... it's ok. You make sure you back it up," said Machado Garry. "I don't know whatever story you made up about meeting me... I've never encountered that story. Listen, you are a good fighter. Show up. Keep winning and you can do anything. You have got massive fights in this division.

"You have got me, you have got (Carlos) Prates, you have got Islam (Makhachev). Show up and fight. You are an animal, you are strong. I don't know any story where I have met you and chat s*** to you. In this sport, if people talk s***, I ignore. Spread good, do good. You have knocked people out, you beat people up, that's what gets respect."

Morales remains undefeated in 19 professional fights, and looks set to be next in line for a crack at Makhachev's coveted gold strap. The 27-year-old knockout artist announced his name on the world stage in his last outing after stopping Sean Brady in the first round last November.

As for Machado Garry, the youngster will now head back to the drawing board in a bid to work his way back into title contention. Reacting to the defeat, he told Joe Rogan: "Nothing surprised me. I have nothing but respect for Islam. I believed in my heart and in my soul I was better than him tonight; he won, I have no complaints, no excuses.

Article continues below

“This was the best camp of my life. I love my wife, my little boy, I fight to make them happy. I’m 28 years of age, I have a decade of domination in this sport. This man won today, that’s okay. I’m as f***ing bulletproof as I could be up here [mentally]. To all the fans that doubt me, I’ll be back. I don’t need any of you, so go f*** yourselves!”

In a later video uploaded to his social media, Machado Garry stated: "Tonight wasn't my night. Islam was just better than me tonight and that's okay. I just fought arguably the greatest fighter we've ever seen, and I pushed him to the f****** wire. I'm so proud of myself."

Sports.title: Dana White tears into Ian Machado Garry with brutal five-word assessment
Sports.content:
Dana White tears into Ian Machado Garry with brutal five-word assessment

UFC boss Dana White did not hold back in his assessment of Ian Machado Garry immediately after the Irishman's defeat to Islam Makhachev on Saturday night

View Image UFC boss Dana White was left stunned by Ian Machado Garry during his fight with Islam Makhachev (Image: Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)

UFC supremo Dana White was left far from impressed with Ian Machado Garry's antics heading into the final round of the Irishman's fight with Islam Makhachev.

‌



The Dublin scrapper took on Makhachev in his first title fight in the UFC on Saturday night over in Philadelphia. Makhachev would go on to dominate the majority of the early proceedings, but after a spirited comeback in the third and fourth rounds, the title contest was neck and neck in the final round.

‌



Rather than attempt to stamp his authority in the fifth stanza, Machado Garry rushed to the centre of the canvas and hugged his rival before they eventually split and traded leather for the final five minutes. It was the Russian champion who would go on to get the nod on points - his first successful defence as a 170lb champion.

‌



But boss White was not happy with Machado Garry's respectful gesture at all. "I think Ian is a talented guy. If he had even an ounce of killer instinct, in that fifth round, you don't come out and hug and shake hands. That s*** drives me crazy. You come out in that fifth round with a flying knee and try to finish the fight," he said at the post-fight press conference.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



UFC star dies aged 34 after suffering suspected heart attack READ MORE :

Makhachev was later quick to echo White's sentiments, stating: "Bro I don't understand. This is a fight, we don't have to hug each other every round. We're going to war. I respect all my opponents, but Ian respects too much. It's not something you have to play. This is fight, this is not game."

The Russian brawler made history at UFC 330 after he broke Anderson Silva's record for the longest win streak in UFC history (17). Speaking about the historic victory with Khabib Nurmagomedov in his corner, Makhachev said: “Ian is a great fighter, he gave me a hard time. But I prove every fight.

Conor McGregor demands Max Holloway fight result is changed READ MORE :

"Oh, let’s see [if it’s the most-difficult fight I’ve had]. Maybe the first one in Australia [against Alex Volkanovski], it was also very hard. I feel the guys have more power [at 170lb], very hard to submit them, but still my game is working. I take down all my opponents and give them a hard time there."

Article continues below

Despite suffering his second career defeat, Machado Garry was rather gracious following the loss. "Nothing surprised me. I have nothing but respect for Islam," he said. "I believed in my heart and in my soul I was better than him tonight; he won, I have no complaints, no excuses.

“This was the best camp of my life. I love my wife, my little boy, I fight to make them happy. I’m 28 years of age, I have a decade of domination in this sport. This man won today, that’s okay. I’m as f***ing bulletproof as I could be up here [mentally]. To all the fans that doubt me, I’ll be back. I don’t need any of you, so go f*** yourselves!”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta fired Community Shield warning as predictions made for Arsenal vs Man City
Sports.content:
The Community Shield is here! And this time it might count for a little more.

The curtain-raiser at Wembley has never been a fixture to get the juices flowing, but this time it is Arsenal vs Manchester City in a match which will see two of the favourites for the Premier League title lock horns.

Mikel Arteta has been enduring a largely frustrating pre-season, with Arsenal shipping goals in friendlies and unable to land their biggest targets in the transfer window. Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis are the only two major additions so far but could feature on Sunday.

City, meanwhile, are at the start of the long-awaited post-Pep Guardiola Enzo Maresca era. They have signed Elliot Anderson, but could lose Rodri in a transfer tussle with Barcelona.

‌



That is the context for the 3pm kick-off. Now read what Mirror Football's writers think will happen.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Nathan Ridley

It was always going to be a tricky summer for Arsenal given their gruelling 2025-26 campaign and the World Cup that followed. How do you improve a title-winning squad without breaking the bank?

They went for Vinicius Junior. They went for Morgan Rogers. But you can't blame Arsenal for A. not being Real Madrid and B. deciding not to spend £116million on an attacker who wouldn't be guaranteed a place in their line-up?

‌



Mikel Arteta didn't have much time to work with his regular starters in pre-season and it showed. The Gunners leaked goals like we haven't seen for years.

View 4 Images Arsenal have got used to picking the ball out of their net in pre-season (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

And I'm expecting Manchester City to capitalise on that rustiness, with Erling Haaland hungry to exploit Arsenal's lack of a first-choice centre-back pairing. When it comes to the title race, however, I reckon Arsenal's muscle memory will be enough to see them through in a season full of unknowns, especially when it comes to the top teams and their new managers.

Prediction: Arsenal 1-2 Manchester City

‌



Ben Husband

Here we go then, the game that will undoubtedly create the biggest over-reactions that ultimately don’t come true.

With so many players yet to be up to full speed after the World Cup, this game - and the result - should be taken with a huge pinch of salt. But Arsenal have looked a little rusty in pre-season and William Saliba's absence has made them look a little more susceptible at the back.

Erling Haaland is yet to play in pre-season, but it usually doesn't take him long to get back to full speed and I expect him to have some involvement - and to inevitably score.

The Gunners will be much stronger once they have their full arsenal (sorry) available, but this weekend I fancy City to get one over their title rivals.

‌



Prediction: Arsenal 1-2 Manchester City

View 4 Images Erling Haaland was given extra time off after the World Cup (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Felix Keith

The last three Community Shields have finished as a draw, treating the Wembley crowd to a penalty shoot-out and I can see this going the same way.

‌



Having gone through an array of friendlies in pre-season, this curtain-raiser is only a step up in terms of competitiveness. However, the rivalry between the two clubs and the impending title race should add a bit more to the occasion.

City are at the early stages of the Maresca era and will likely take a little longer to gel than Arsenal, who are much the same as last season currently, due to a sluggish transfer window. It's hard to read too much into pre-season results, where Arsenal have been slack defensively, so I think they'll up the ante enough to win, but only just.

Prediction: Arsenal 1-1 Manchester City (Arsenal win on penalties)

View 4 Images William Saliba is a big miss for Arsenal (Image: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images)

‌



Dan Marsh

Arsenal's rock-solid defence was the cornerstone of their Premier League title win last season, but it feels like their strength in that area will be tested with William Saliba out long-term and no signings in that area as we stand.

Manchester City can take advantage of that here, although their pre-season preparations have also been hampered by players returning to action later due to the World Cup. Enzo Maresca's arrival has seen City's wingers play wider than they did under Pep Guardiola in their warm-up games, so it feels like they will be given a license to really get at Arsenal's full-backs.

I think Maresca will carry on Guardiola's fine work and winning today's game would be the ideal start for him. I think it will be tight and not particularly fluent. And City will edge it 2-1.

‌



Prediction: Arsenal 1-2 Manchester City

Sports.title: Tonda Eckert's Spygate explanation, why Southampton didn't sack him and intern's new job
Sports.content:
Tonda Eckert's Spygate explanation, why Southampton didn't sack him and intern's new job

Southampton's Championship campaign gets underway against Watford on Sunday, with questions abound as to why Tonda Eckert is still in charge

View 3 Images Tonda Eckert is set to lead Southampton in their Championship opener despite all the Spygate fallout (Image: X/SouthamptonFC)

Tonda Eckert will be the man in the spotlight when Southampton return to Championship duties on Sunday. The Saints might have found themselves back among the heights of the Premier League this season but instead open away to Watford a week earlier.

‌



Last season's Spygate farce saw Southampton exiled from the Championship play-off final. Losing semi-finalists Middlesbrough took their place at Wembley but couldn't make it count against Hull City, who won the race for the third and final promotion place.

‌



The dust may have settled but the effects are very much still being felt today as Southampton start the season with a four-point deduction. There's also the possibility that Eckert will face a touchline ban - or worse - after being charged with misconduct by the FA.

‌



He even sat in the stands for one pre-season fixture as a trial run. Mirror Football examines the ongoing fallout from one of the biggest controversies in English football history as Southampton go again.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Spygate explanation

Back in May, Boro lobbied a very serious accusation that a member of Southampton's staff had been spotted at their Rockliffe training ground recording a team session. The man in question was seen recording footage from behind a tree but fled via the adjoining golf club after he was confronted by Middlesbrough staff and refused to identify himself.

‌



Boro's suspicions proved accurate as Southampton analyst intern William Salt was found to be the man in question. The Saints were charged with breaking EFL regulations 3.4 and 127.1 and ultimately admitted to an Independent Disciplinary Commission that they had conducted similar acts of espionage prior to games against Oxford and Ipswich Town earlier that same season, having initially denied spying.

EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate READ MORE :

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal READ MORE :

An arbitration panel reached the conclusion that Southampton had launched "a contrived and determined plan from top down to gain a competitive advantage”" over their competition. However, it took some of the responsibility off the analysts who watched opposition training, surmising that they "felt pressurised" to do so.

On May 19, a full week after Southampton's play-off semi-final victory over Boro, Southampton's expulsion from the final was confirmed. Kim Hellberg's men were reinstated in their place and Eckert was left to rue his error in judgement as a dream first season at St Mary's ended in nightmarish fashion.

‌



Explaining the saga, the German made the argument he was used to similar practices being acceptable in his homeland and Italy, where he'd gained much of his coaching experience. Eckert contended that he was not aware this was against EFL laws having taken charge in his first senior role midway through the season, though that wouldn't necessarily explain why Saints analysts had been quite so covert in their operations.

"I am a young coach, I have made a mistake, and I take full responsibility," said Eckert. "I am devastated that after six months of building that relationship [with the fans] back up, the season has come to an end...come to an end that couldn’t have left us in a worse place than we are in right now."

‌



He added: "None of what has happened had any effect on the sporting performance...I hope that over time you can understand and forgive."

Eckert, 33, confirmed earlier in the summer that he had received death threats and had no choice but to involve the police. The Athletic has also reported he reached out to former England manager Gareth Southgate and the pair had a "long conversation" so that Eckert could better understand the FA's rules.

Why he's still at Saints

View 3 Images Dragan Solak has stood by Eckert - but told him not to make a similar mistake again (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

‌



Many might make the argument that Eckert's dismissal should not have been a decision that was left to Southampton's discretion. As it is, however, the south-coast side were allowed to pass judgement on the matter and ultimately decided to stick by their boss.

It wasn't just the owners who made that call, either. The Athletic recently reported the club's board surveyed the playing squad for their opinion the day after Southampton's appeal against their play-off expulsion was rejected - and the answer was that Eckert be allowed to stay on and make things right.

On the same day Saints owner Dragan Solak confirmed the club was sticking with Eckert, the latter posted a video explaining his actions. That also included an apology to the supporters for the manner in which his deception had led to the club suffering such extreme punishment.

‌



While Solak has proved forgiving over the ordeal, he isn't entirely without fury concerning Eckert's future. And the Serb has confirmed he has already warned his manager not to let something like this befall his club again as he gives him a "deserved second chance."

“I told him, ‘You almost broke my heart,'" said Solak earlier this summer. "'You do it again, you’ll kill me. The next time I see you in July, if you don’t know the EFL book of rules by heart, you can’t work for me. Because, we can’t have another mistake.' I truly hope that he will learn from this experience and he will achieve an incredible career."

Eckert's reputation among the fans may be somewhat more divided after it was ultimately his choices that led to the promotion dream crashing down last season. However, it's evident he has many backers from all sections of the club's hierarchy inside St. Mary's.

‌



Intern's new job

View 3 Images Southampton spy William Salt was identified via a photo posted on the club's official website (Image: Southampton FC)

As for Salt, he is an intern no more. In fact, his role in the debacle has led to a promotion after the Daily Mail reported he's landed himself a permanent job in Southampton's academy.

Eckert was reportedly impressed by Salt's work at the club despite his role in the Spygate mess. And they've stuck by him with a more cemented role at their Staplewood training ground.

Article continues below

Salt will presumably be permitted to continue studying under one of the hottest young coaching talents in Europe as a result. However, there's one very specific page in Eckert's book that the former intern will not be taking a leaf out of anytime soon.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
