World.title: Latest OUTLOOK for SASSA Children’s Grants in September 2026
World.content:
SASSA Children’s Grants in September 2026 is the most comprehensive social-welfare protection paid out by the National Treasury. Image: File

We’re looking ahead to SASSA Children’s Grants in September 2026, just under three weeks’ away from payment.

With over 13-million recipients, South Africa’s child-welfare system represents the most expensive social protection in the country.

Therefore, millions of households with vulnerable children should diaries this date – Thursday, 3 September 2026.



SASSA CHILDREN’S GRANTS IN SEPTEMBER 2026

SASSA minister Dina Pule has come out admitting that beneficiaries are being underserved under the current agency regime. Image: File

Encouragingly, the gap between payments represents a normal 28-day cycle and not the 33 days it did previously. As ever, the grant amounts for SASSA Children’s Grants in September 2026 themselves are unchanged:

Child Support pays R580 , up by R20 from R560 back in April 2026.

, up by from R560 back in April 2026. Foster Child pays R1 290 , up by R40 from R1 250 back in April 2026.

, up by from R1 250 back in April 2026. Care Dependency pays R2 400 up by R80 from R2 320 back in April 2026.

Therefore, if you register your child with the Department of Home Affairs from the month of their birth, you can start claiming child welfare immediately (if you qualify). Calculated all the way to their 18th birthday, this is a benefit of roughly R185 000 (adjusted for inflation) to the parents.

INCOME ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

Likewise, applicants should know the revised income eligibility requirements from the South African Social Security Agency. Previously, a single caregiver on Child Support could earn R5 100 per month and still qualify. Now that limit has increased to R5 800. While, for married couples looking after a minor, the figure increases from R10 200 to R11 600 per month.



Tallied up annually, that is R69 600 (single person) and R139 200 (couple). Note that there is no asset portion to the means test, like with SASSA Old-Age Grants.

On a positive note, the agency also claims new maximum wait times of 90 minutes at SASSA offices and, in some cases, same-day service for applicants.

Thanks to self-service kiosks with Wi-Fi, beneficiaries can complete eLife and biometric verification in double-quick time and for free. The agency also says it is tackling the scourge of criminal syndicates and vigilantes that are extorting vulnerable beneficiaries waiting in SASSA queues. Read all about the five things affecting SASSA grants in September 2026 HERE.



SAME-DAY SERVICE FOR SASSA CHILD SUPPORT GRANTS

Independent research confirms that SASSA Children’s Grants have saved millions of newborns from malnutrition. Image: File

Previously, the waiting period for approval to be closer to three months. However, if you have all your documents in order on your first visit, you could walk away with an approved grant right there and then. Here’s what you need to bring to your application appointment:

Valid identity documents (IDs) and birth certificates of you, your child and spouse (if married).

Proof of marital status (marriage, birth or death certificate of your spouse).

Proof of income (you and your spouse).

Certified three-month bank statement, not older than three months.

bank statement, not older than three months. Proof of address (a utility statement with your name on it that’s not more the three-months old).

If you don’t produce all the correct documents and copies, you may be sent away and asked to return. And if you are denied a SASSA grant, you have three months to lodge an appeal with the DSD HERE.

You can contact SASSA through the following channels for more information:



SASSA Toll-Free Call: 0800 60 10 11

SASSA Head Office: 012 400 2322

Email SASSA: grantenquiries@sassa.gov.za

Visit the SASSA Service portal HERE

Beyond SASSA Children’s Grants in September 2026, the next thing to look forward to is the prospect of mid-cycle increases in October 2026. Although these figures are still to be confirmed by the National Treasury, and often exclude Child Support (but not the others).

But what do you think? Do you have anything to report ahead of SASSA Children’s Grants in September 2026? How are you finding the agency’s service? Let us know in the comments section below …

World.title: ‘You deserve it all’: Minister Gwarube spoils assistant with birthday goodies!
World.content:
On 12 August, Siviwe Gwarube, the Minister of Basic Education, pleasantly surprised her long-serving assistant, Shannon Malan, with birthday goodies.

MINISTER SIVIWE GWARUBE GIFTS ASSISTANT ON HER BIRTHDAY

The Instagram reel opens with the minister whispering into the camera, “I’ve got a surprise for the birthday girl. Come with me.”

She then walks down the office hallway with birthday goodies in hand. After entering Shannon’s office, the minister happily sings the birthday song and gives her the gift.



So, what was in the orange paper bag? The minister bought her a fancy kettle from Le Creuset, matching salt and pepper shakers, a balloon, and a handwritten card that reads, “Happy birthday. Thank you for all that you do for me. I love you.”

After receiving her birthday gift, Shannon said, “I love you so much, my ma’am. Thank you very much.”

MINISTER: ‘SHE RUNS MY LIFE’

In her birthday message to Shannon, the minister revealed they’ve been joined at the hip for almost a decade. Shannon started working as her assistant when she was the DA’s chief whip. However, managing her as a minister has proven to be quite challenging for Shannon.

“Shannon and I have been working together for 9 years. Almost a whole decade. She became my assistant when I was the Chief Whip of the Official Opposition. I’ve never looked back. But her most demanding and challenging job has to be managing *me* as a Minister,” she wrote.

The minister also praised Shannon for managing all facets of her life with the precision of a “Japanese train”, adding that even her family knows her.



“She runs my life like a Japanese train. Professionally and personally. My family knows her by name. My greatest achievements. They have been shared with her,” she added.

Lastly, the minister expressed deep gratitude for Shannon’s presence in her life, declaring she deserves all the spoils in the world.

“I’m so grateful for her. And any chance I get to spoil her, I’ll do it. As a reminder that she followed me to the edge of the cliff and jumped with me into the most uncertain and terrifying journey yet. Happy Birthday, my Love. You deserve it all!” she wrote.

World.title: ‘Voetsek!’: All Blacks supporters at Loftus put on blast
World.content:
All Blacks fans at Loftus. Images via Instagram

South African All Blacks supporters at Loftus Versfeld – where the New Zealand national team played the Bulls – were met with scathing remarks on social media.

The Kiwis won their third consecutive match in the Greatest Rivalry series, beating the Bulls 50-19.

The ABs have a large supporter base in South Africa, particularly in the Western Cape.



ALL BLACKS SUPPORTERS AT LOFTUS PUT ON BLAST

On social media, images and video clips of crowds of rugby fans at Loftus Stadium – some of whom were All Blacks supporters – had South African social media users riled up.

On the official Instagram account for the Greatest Rivalry Series, a group of locals held up a sign that read: “Adopt us. We’re South African, but our hearts are Kiwi”.

The post was captioned: “All Blacks fans are out in full force in Pretoria”



Outside New Zealand, the All Blacks have the strongest support in South Africa, particularly among the coloured community in the Western Cape. For many, the support is deep-rooted in Apartheid, when New Zealand stood with non-white players who were sidelined from joining the Springboks.

Under the post, the supporters were met with comments like…

“If you don’t support the country you live in, then go and live in the country you support”



“Voetsek, kindly then. Go well”

“Seriously? Go live in New Zealand”

“I’ve never seen white South Africans support All Blacks”



“Supporting the All Blacks is one thing. Holding up a sign saying your “heart isn’t South African” while living in South Africa is just embarrassing. Rivalry is fun. This is cringe”.

WHAT’S NEXT IN THE GREATEST RIVALRY SERIES?

The All Blacks have wrapped up three victories against the Stormers, Sharks and the Bulls.



They will take on the Lions next on 26 August at Ellis Park, Johannesburg.

New Zealand will also take on the Springboks in four test matches in the coming weeks.

22 August – Springboks vs All Blacks – Ellis Park, Johannesburg

29 August – Springboks vs ABs – DHL Stadium, Cape Town

5 September – Springboks vs ABs – FNB Stadium, Johannesburg

12 September – Springboks vs ABs -M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore, USA

World.title: Gayton McKenzie accused of another ‘insensitive’ post
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has been criticised for two recent social media posts. Images via Facebook

Gayton McKenzie has been accused of making another “insensitive” post about a member of the Democratic Alliance.

The Patriotic Alliance leader – who is also the Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture – often uses his platform to call out the party helmed by Geordin Hill-Lewis, particularly over ward territory in the Western Cape.

Like the DA, the PA is also a part of the government of national unity (GNU),



GAYTON MCKENZIE ACCUSED OF AGEIST TWEET TOWARDS HELEN ZILLE

On his X account, Gayton McKenzie was accused of taking an ageist jab at Helen Zille, the DA’s mayoral candidate for Johannesburg.

The PA leader responded to a tweet that claimed that the was “two steps closer to Joburg mayorship”

Gayton responded: “She is one step closer to the graveyard at this age”.

In the comments section, many users found Gayton’s comment distasteful, particularly during Women’s Month. Others reminded the minister of his own past as a reformed convict.

@MrJLabuschagne: “Highly distasteful comment. You are losing traction and support because your ego is growing and your results aren’t keeping up”.

@IsoshalikaZulu: “Whatever your views are about @helenzille, this is distasteful language, especially coming from a sitting Minister. Be exemplary considering your past”



@Truter_Johan: “Tact clearly wasn’t part of the gangster-to-minister career development programme“.

She is one step closer to the graveyard at this age. https://t.co/sv7FRG7yoo — Gayton McKenzie (@GaytonMcK) August 13, 2026

MINISTER DELETES POST ABOUT DA MEMBER WHO DIED

A day later, after taking a jab at Helen Zille, Gayton McKenzie was criticised for making another social media post.

On Facebook, the PA president posted a picture of a DA-branded vehicle that had been involved in a car accident. The fatal crash claimed the life of DA activist, Mviki Ncapayi.

Without knowing about the fatality, Gayton warned DA members to “keep our names our your mouths”

Gayton – who shared “We are glad no one is injured” – also made a Biblical reference, adding “Touch not the anointed”.

The minister’s post was criticised by several DA members, including former PA MP Liam Jacobs, who labelled it “insensitive and fundamentally unsettling”.

Gayton responded on Facebook: “We deleted the post. The person in the bakkie passed away at the hospital, by the time I wrote the post, there have been no news of anyone injured. We sympathise with his family”

Chastising the DA for “lying” and “politicising the death of a man”, he added: “We can never rejoice in the death of anyone”.

He added, “Don’t throw stones when you live in a glass house. The war has started. We are ready to meet you at the ballot. You talk about PA, you will hear from us”

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs star dedicates Man of the Match award to ZCC
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs midfielder Siphesihle Ndlovu dedicated his Man of the Match award to the Zion Christian Church (ZCC) after producing a dominant display against Mamelodi Sundowns.

The Soweto giants held the Brazilians to a 1-1 draw at FNB Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Betway Premiership, with Ndlovu playing a key role in the result.

The hard-tackling midfielder marshalled the Kaizer Chiefs midfield and played a crucial part in their opening goal. Ndlovu held off the Sundowns pressure before setting up Langelihle Phili, who fired Chiefs into the lead in the 63rd minute.



His impressive performance was recognised after the final whistle when he was named Man of the Match.

Speaking after the game, Ndlovu dedicated the individual award to the ZCC, a church he is affiliated with.

“This means a lot to me. I want to dedicate this to the ZCC, where I come from. Jehovah is powerful,” Ndlovu said.  Kaizer Chiefs hold off Sundowns

The Chiefs midfielder also explained how a tactical adjustment helped Amakhosi find a way through against a Sundowns side that dominated possession for large periods of the match.

“It is never an easy match. Sundowns move the ball and make you shift from side to side. You have to be patient and wait for your moment. You are going to get it eventually,” Ndlovu told SABC Sport.

“I did what we needed to do, especially in the midfield.”



Kaizer Chiefs bossed the midfield

Ndlovu added that Amakhosi had to remain adaptable as Sundowns changed their approach throughout the match.

“It’s all tactical. If they change, we need to change. Obviously, we have good analysis. They see that and inform us on time, and we have to adapt quickly,” he explained.

The draw means Kaizer Chiefs remain top of the Betway Premiership standings with seven points from their opening three matches.



With Ndlovu emerging as one of the standout performers against Sundowns, his contribution could prove important as Chiefs look to maintain their strong start to the campaign.

Out of 10, how much do you rate Ndlovu’s performance?

World.title: EXCLUSIVE | CCTV footage shows alleged Reiger Park shooter “was at home”
World.content:
BOKSBURG - Alleged Reiger Park killer Regan Collis' family has provided some footage, asserting that the 23-year-old was at home at the time of the deadly shooting.

The family insists Collis is being framed by a rival gang.

He's accused of killing four people including two Gauteng Anti-Gang Unit officers earlier this month.

He appeared in the Boksburg Magistrate's Court last week, facing four counts of murder and several other serious charges.

Police alleged Collis is a known gangster and that he was out on bail.

Collis was remanded in custody and will be back in court next week for bail application.

Police are adamant he has a case to answer.

The three victims have been buried while the fourth is being laid to rest in Limpopo today.

World.title: Reiger Park Shooting | Constable Thapelo Tlometsane funeral underway
World.content:
ZEBEDIELA – Senior members of the South African Police Service have travelled to Limpopo to join the family of the slain Constable Thapelo Tlometsane to bid him farewell.

Tlometsane, a police officer attached to the Anti-Gang Unit, was killed in an ambush shooting in Reiger Park.

He was killed with his colleague, Constable Siphiwe Sibeko, as they were responding to a shooting in that community.

Two civilians were also killed that night.

Mourners described as courageous, committed and selfless in service.

Also in attendance are Police Deputy Minister, Dr Polly Boshielo and the Acting National Commissioner of the SAPS, Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane.

World.title: ‘Expensive talk shops’ won’t solve SADC’s deeper problems - expert
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - International summits have to result in change instead of being expensive talk shops.

That's the view of International Relations expert Professor Anthoni van Nieuwkerk.

As the SADC summit gets under way in Durban, Van Nieuwerk said the regional body should strengthen the spirit of cooperation between its member states.

"We were united as a region when we fought apartheid and colonialism, which brought independence to South Africa, to Namibia, and so on. We've lost that energy and that momentum and we have to recreate that.

“It cannot be that only heads of state, presidents, and prime ministers represent 350 million people in Southern Africa. There's a crisis in Zambia with the election. There's election violence. It happened last year in Mozambique.

“It happened the year before in Tanzania. There's a military coup in Madagascar. We have problems elsewhere in the region. Now, I don't think politicians have all the answers and heads of state, when they talk to each other, they take the blue lights, they go to a VIP venue in Durban in this case, and they talk to each other as friends. That is not going to solve the deeper problems that we face in the region."

World.title: Kay Motsepe Schools Championship invests R1.4m in community projects
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Kay Motsepe Schools Championship continues to create opportunities for young South Africans on and off the field.

What started as a schools' football tournament more than two decades ago has grown into one of the country's leading youth development platforms.

Now celebrating 22 years of impact, the championship brings together learners from across South Africa through football, netball and choral music.

The netball competition has become a key feature of the Championship, showcasing the country's top under-15 girls' teams.

A total of R1,4million is available in prize funding but importantly the rewards are not paid out in cash.

Instead, the winning schools select legacy projects in their communities, ensuring the benefits extend well beyond the final whistle.

World.title: ‘This is a big loss’ –  KZN MEC pays tribute to Scebi Dlamini
World.content:
UMSINGA - Friends, family, fellow Maskandi artists and fans laid artist Scebi Dlamini to rest.

The 29-year-old was being laid to rest in his hometown of Msinga, in KZN.

Dlamini died in a car crash in Richards Bay last Sunday, while on his way to perform at a festival. Dlamini died with Sipho "Gupta" Mchunu, his backup singer and stage crew member.

Mntomuhle Khawula, the Provincial MEC for Sports, Arts and Culture attended the funeral, he said the industry has lost one of its greatest.

“Indeed, the whole province of KZN, the country and the industry are grieving this big loss. The kind of talent that has come out of uMsinga is amazing. Condolences to the Mchunu and Dlamini families and to the whole area of uMsinga and uMzinyathi.”

World.title: ACDP promises clean governance and ‘new crop’ of leaders
World.content:
BENONI - The ACDP has launched its 2026 Local Government Elections Manifesto.

The party's outlined its plans ahead of the November polls.

Their leader Reverend Kenneth Meshoe said the party will bring a new crop of leaders focused on accountability and clean governance.

“Well, they have the right to lose hope with the current crop of leaders they have. But now with the ACDP, they will be having a different crop of individuals, people who are capable, and people who keep their weight.

“So a promise is that South Africa will not remain the same. If they put us in those offices, they elect our mayoral candidates, then they will see. They will ask themselves the question, why did we wait so long?” Meshoe said.

World.title: Reiger Park Shooting | “He was preparing for the future’ – Dimpane reflects on slain officer’s career
World.content:
REIGER PARK - Acting National Police Commissioner Puleng Dimpane described Anti-Gang Unit Constable Siphiwe Sibeko as a young officer dedicated to continuous learning and professional growth.

Sibeko was killed in Reiger Park last week.

At his funeral, Dimpane highlighted Sibeko’s extensive training during nearly seven years in the police service.

She said he was preparing for greater responsibility and the challenges ahead.

“These were not merely courses recorded on his personal file. They reflected a young police officer who understood that professional policing demands continuous learning discipline as well as preparedness.

“Significantly in May this year, only months before his death, Constable Sibeko successfully completed further maintenance shooting training in handgun as well as rifle. He was preparing himself for the future. He was sharpening his skills. He was maintaining his operational readiness. He was doing what a committed police officer does, preparing for the next call, the next shift and the next challenge,” Dimpane said.

World.title: ‘I imagined he’d sing at my wedding’ – fan mourns Scebi Dlamini’s passing
World.content:
UMSINGA - Fans remember Scebi Dlamini as a Maskandi superstar and a humble soul offstage.

Dlamini is being laid to rest in uMsinga, KwaZulu-Natal.

He died in a car crash last Sunday in Richards Bay, en route to a festival performance.

One fan said she loved Dlamini so much, she would have loved to have him perform at her wedding.

“I love the song Bengidakiwe because I always imagined that he would sing at my wedding. His music represented women,” she said.

Another fan said: “I have been a fan of Scebi since I started following Maskandi music. I admired his humility and it taught me the value of being loved for who you are. He brought us authentic, old-school Maskandi. His loss cuts deep.”

Dlamini’s death has also affected other fans in their personal lives.

“I learned of his death on Facebook that he had died, and my heart broke. For the entire week, I have been struggling to cope at work.”

World.content:

World.title: Gachagua: We will protect ourselves against goons
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua addresses residents of Naivasha where he lashed out at President William and told him to keep of former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [Antony Gitonga, Standard]

Former Deputy President and DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua has vowed to fight back against goons allegedly disrupting his political rallies, saying his supporters will defend themselves if the police fail to protect them.

Speaking during the opening of DCP offices in Nakuru, Gachagua said they had received intelligence that the National Police Service (NPS) had been instructed to keep off areas where his rallies were being held.

Gachagua spoke a day after goons attacked his convoy at Kaptembwo in Nakuru West Sub-County, forcing him to abandon a DCP campaign rally and flee the scene alongside other leaders.

Six vehicles belonging to leaders, including Ol-Kalou MP Samuel Waweru, were vandalised during the incident as DCP leaders and supporters scrambled for safety.

Gachagua accused President William Ruto of allegedly planning the chaos through a Nakuru MP who, he claimed, had paid goons to disrupt his rallies.

“President William Ruto planned the chaos using a Nakuru MP who paid goons to attack us. This was despite his assurance that our campaign rallies would be protected,” Gachagua said.

He claimed he had received credible intelligence that police officers had been advised to keep away from Kaptembwo during the attack.

Gachagua further alleged that although the MP was associated with the Jubilee Party, he was being used by President Ruto to cause chaos.

“I have also spoken to Jubilee Party leaders to put their house in order. If it is proven that the MP is being used by the President, then he should be removed. That will inform how we relate to the Jubilee Party,” he said.

The former Deputy President said goons had allegedly been deployed to cause chaos at various stopovers, but some police officers who were unhappy with the Kenya Kwanza administration had provided his team with intelligence.

“We stood down our guard, hoping for protection from the government, but we are now on high alert and we will protect ourselves,” Gachagua said.

He also accused senior police officers in Nakuru of allegedly working with goons to disrupt his rallies.

According to Gachagua, junior police officers were unhappy with being allegedly forced to work with goons to cause chaos, steal property and kill Kenyans.

“These police officers have reduced salaries, they are not funded, they lack fuel and they are suffering,” he said.

World.title: That's just wishful thinking, Gachagua mocks Ruto's 'must-win' 2027 claim
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua during a rally in Nakuru. [Rigahi Gachagua, Facebook]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed President William Ruto's declaration that his coalition "must win" the 2027 General Election, calling it wishful thinking.

Gachagua made the remarks on his DCP TV platform during a tour of Nakuru County that took in Free Area and Kanu House in Nakuru Town East, among other stops, hours after the party said his convoy came under attack in Kaptembwa, Nakuru Town West.

DCP claimed in videos posted on its official platforms that Gachagua "survived an assassination attempt after narrowly escaping a bullet by goons," though it did not provide further details on the circumstances of the incident.

Addressing a public engagement in Nakuru Town East, Gachagua condemned the disruption. "Political violence will not cure the already deteriorating support of our opponents. It is shameful to organise goons to disrupt peaceful meetings," he said.

Turning to Ruto's pledge at last week's Naivasha retreat that his broad-based UDA-ODM coalition "must win" 2027, Gachagua argued the claim was unsupported by the opposition's landslide victory in last month's Ol Kalou by-election.

"So when William Ruto says that he must win, that is just wishful thinking," he said, adding, “If William Ruto had his way, he would continue lying to the people of Kenya."

He noted that Ruto's allies had predicted an 80 per cent win in Ol Kalou, only for the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) candidate to lose the Nyandarua seat by a similar margin to DCP's Sammy Waweru Ngotho on July 17.

"He is saying it is a must as who," Gachagua said. "He must persuade the people of Kenya that they can trust him, that they can believe him. But he has lied to the people of Kenya. Nobody trusts him anymore."

The Kaptembwa incident is the latest in a string of attacks DCP has blamed on state-linked "goons" since Gachagua's October 2024 impeachment, including a stoning of his campaign truck in Gilgil in July and clashes at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) in August 2025.

Gachagua has repeatedly accused security agencies of orchestrating the violence, allegations the government has previously denied.

World.title: Ruto accuses Uhuru of failed projects, sponsoring opposition
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto at Maili Nne, Huruma and Eldoret City in Uasin Gishu County. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused his predecessor, retired President Uhuru Kenyatta, whom he portrayed as a sponsor of some of his political opponents.

Speaking to residents of Maili Nne, Huruma and Eldoret City in Uasin Gishu County, Ruto questioned Uhuru's record on affordable housing, Universal Health Coverage and education, challenging Kenyans to compare the former administration’s record with his government’s programmes.

“Yule sponsor wao si alishindwa na maneno ya affordable housing, si alishindwa na mambo ya universal health coverage, si alishindwa na maneno ya kusomesha watoto wetu?” Ruto said.

Ruto takes aim at Uhuru, accuses predecessor of failed promises and backing opposition proxies pic.twitter.com/GeJgEastoJ — The Standard Digital (@StandardKenya) August 13, 2026

He also accused his opponents of lacking a clear policy agenda and urged voters to demand details of their plans before supporting them.

“Wale watu mumesikia mpango yao, agenda yao, mumesikia sera yao, mumesikia maono yao?” he asked.

The President said the 2027 contest should be based on what political leaders have delivered and what they intend to do for Kenyans, rather than slogans or calls for his removal from office.

Ruto said voters should reject attempts by politicians to win support by simply demanding that he leaves office after one term without presenting clear policies, programmes and an alternative agenda.

"Kila kiongozi anapimwa na ile kazi amefanya. Hakuna mtu atakuja kututapeli hapa ati atuambie ‘Kasongo must go’, ati one term, halafu tumpatie kazi,” Ruto said.

The President challenged residents to scrutinise the track records of politicians seeking to replace his administration in the 2027 elections.

“Nyinyi watu wa Eldoret si mumewahi piga kura? Si nyinyi ni mafundi wa siasa? Si mnajua hawa viongozi wote?” he asked.

His remarks come amid recent accusations by a section of Kenya Kwanza leaders that the retired Head of State is financing the Linda Mwananchi movement and the overall Opposition.

However, the Linda Mwananchi brigade led by Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna dismissed the allegations, saying Uhuru's involvement is limited to publicly encouraging young people to take up leadership.

World.title: Court dismisses bid to strike out duty-free rice import case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi issued a gazette notice allowing the importation of 500,000 metric tons of duty-free milled white rice. [Courtesy]

The High Court has declined to strike out a case challenging the government’s decision to allow duty-free rice into the country.

Justice Edward Muriithi, in his ruling, said that the case by Kirinyaga Senator Kamau Murango was weighty as it questions the legitimacy of the government’s interest to ensure food security in the country as measured against the legitimate expectation that they would sell their products without losses owing to flooding of exported commodities.

“It would appear that this apparent intersection (or conflict) of rights caused by the Cabinet Secretary for Treasury in repeatedly publishing the Gazette Notices subject of the constitutional challenge herein and in other suits gives rise to questions in terms of Article 165(4) whether it was a valid exercise of authority within the meaning of the Constitution and whether the Gazette authority to import rice duty-free infringes upon the farmers’ right to property through resultant price drops affecting the marketability and profitability returns of the local farmers’ rice growing activity,” ruled Justice Muriithi.

This comes as two separate cases were filed questioning the government’s fresh green light to importers to bring into the country 4,900 tons of rice. Rice farmers say the country has more than enough rice to feed Kenyans. They complained that the move was to flood the market.

In the case before Justice Muriithi, the government claimed that the court had no powers to entertain the claims as this was an administrative issue. It also argued that several cases had been filed in different courts, hence, an abuse of court process.

On July 28, 2025, the National Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi issued a gazette notice allowing the importation of 500,000 metric tons of duty-free milled white rice.

The notice has created a circus, with the judiciary as the playing field.

The cases that were filed in different courts tell of a food crop that has turned out to be hotter than a potato.

Kenya produces 244,000 metric tons of rice, against a consumption demand of at least 1 billion. This creates a window for businesses to import rice worth Sh55 billion.

Mbadi allowed duty-free rice because the government needed to close the market gap. However, those opposed to it claim that there is enough rice, and the importation window was made to create a glut in the country, which would harm rice farmers.

So far, the rice import has attracted six cases. The drama, which is now full-blown, has seen Farmers Party opt to drop the case, only for Kirinyaga Senator Kamau Murango and MCA David Mathenge to fight in a bid to salvage it.

The political party claimed the price of grade one rice has been retailing at approximately Sh 355 and Sh 385 per Kg for imported brands and between Sh 166 and Sh 277 for locally produced rice, depending on the variety (pishori, basmati, long grain, biryani) as well as the blend.

It also claimed that the price is fully determined by market forces, as there have not been any duty-free waivers to any importers of Grade 1 rice since November of last year, with the rains being predictable.

In response, Mbadi argued that there was a need to address the rise in the cost of living. He said that the Cabinet approved a framework to position the Kenya National Trading Corporation (KNTC) as the anchor of State initiatives to create a price stabilizer for essential household food items.

According to him, rice is the third most important cereal after maize and wheat. He was of the view that about 1 million metric tons of rice in the country is imported mainly from India, Pakistan and Tanzania.

He asserted that the current retail market price ranges between Sh 190 and Sh 220 per kilogram for Grade 1 milled white rice, representing a significant increase from last year's average of Sh 150 per kilogram during the duty-free period.

He argued that Kenya needs 1.5 million tons of rice to seal the current rice deficit, adding that 95 per cent of the imported rice is basmati, which would allegedly not affect the market for local pishori rice.

Mbadi also cited food security risk in Turkana, Marsabit, North Eastern and Parts of the Coastal area.

Kerugoya High Court Judge Edward Mureithi froze clearance of the consignment.

Nevertheless, he was not the only one who had issued the orders involving the same issue. Miles away from his court, Milimani High Court Judge Chacha Mwita (now a Court of Appeal Judge)had also barred the government from bringing in the rice, in a case filed by Japheth Kirui. This was on October 14 last year.

Following the orders, the Attorney General, the Kenya Bureau of Standards, and the Agriculture Cabinet Secretary lawyers raised concern that there were five other cases filed in Mombasa, Kisumu, Milimani Commercial Court and Kerugoya by different parties, over the same issue.

This prompted Justice Mwita to order that Kirui appear before him in person on October 30, 2025.

When he took the witness box, he told the court that he was born in Kuresoi, but he sells household items at a kiosk in Embakasi.

Asked by the Judge what he knew about the case, he went mute.

AG’s lawyer, Henry Kaumba, told the Judge that Kirui was allegedly being used as a proxy.

“It is doubtful whether the petitioner knows about the case and what transpired and even the development in the proceedings that have taken place. It is unfortunate,” said Kaumba.

In his filed reply, he said 250,000 tonnes had already been shipped into the country, with others on the way in the high seas.

World.title: You have failed Kenyans, Gachagua tells Ruto
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua when he read out President Ruto’s four-year score card during a media briefing at the party’s offices in Nairobi on August 11, 2026. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused President William Ruto of failing Kenyans and abandoning his campaign promises.

Gachagua who was speaking at the DCP headquarters accused the president of eroding democratic gains of multipartyism and swallowing opposition parties.

“Four years later, Mr. William Ruto has betrayed the trust bestowed on him by the people of Kenya, betrayed the fruits and foundation of our Nation that have been built by previous administrations under the various development blue prints such as Vision 2030,” he said.

Gachagua was addressing the press on the score card of the Kenya Kwanza administration for the four years it has been in leadership.

According to the opposition figure, President Ruto had promised to uphold the rule of law, build a secure, just and democratic Kenyan founded on the constitution but he had abandoned all of the promises.

He added that there were promises of professionalising the National Police Service, safeguarding human rights, protecting Kenyans and strengthening the administration of justice while ensuring security agencies are accountable to the constitution.

Gachagua alleged that the Kenya Kwanza administration had allowed goonism and drug abuse to thrive adding that the country had also become a bedrock of extrajudicial killings and an abductors playground.

He said that during campaigns they had promised to amend and operationalise the National Coroners Service Act of 2017 to establish the Coroner General’s office to remove the burden of probing deaths from the regular police channels and Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).

Gachagua said that proposed amendments were aimed at removing potential conflict of interest and ensuring transparency in handling unexplained deaths, enforced disappearances or fatalities caused by the police.

“Four years later, this promise has not been fulfilled.”

He accused the government of overseeing the arrest and rendition of government critics from Turkey, Uganda, Tanzania and South Sudan adding that officials attached to a construction company from China were deported when they protested the awarding of a contract to rivals.

“Kenyans are not safe, our children are not safe, investors are not safe and foreigners are not safe. Foreigners are not safe, Investors are not safe, no one in Kenya is safe.”

He accused the President of limiting the freedom of the press through sponsored disinformation campaigns and also citing the attempted abduction of Standard Group’s Associated Editor Alex Kiprotich in Nakuru on June 26, 2026.

According to Gachagua the government had failed to fight corruption despite promising to do so adding that it had entrenched graft as a way of life in Kenya.

World.title: Wamboka: Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang'i should back Sifuna
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kabuchai Mp Majimbo kalasinga and his counterpart Jack Wamboka during a press briefing on Monday. [Juliet Omelo, Standard]

The political battle for the 2027 presidency has intensified, with leaders allied to the Linda Mwananchi movement urging opposition figures Kalonzo Musyoka, Rigathi Gachagua and Fred Matiang’i to abandon their presidential ambitions and back Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna.

Bumula MP Jack Wamboka made the call after a three-day political tour of Western Kenya by the Linda mwananchi brigade, saying the region had demonstrated growing grassroots support for Sifuna.

Wamboka said the tour was a major success, with close to 22 rallies held in three days. He added that the crowds reflected growing enthusiasm for Sifuna, particularly among young people, women, political aspirants and ordinary voters.

“We respect you, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i. We know you have what it takes but in 2027, we ask you to stand with Sifuna,” Wamboka said.

He said the reception in Western Kenya showed that Sifuna’s campaign was gaining national attention.

The first time MP said Sifuna had focused on issues affecting Western Kenya, particularly the collapse of industries and the struggling sugar sector. He pointed to Mumias and Nzoia sugar factories, saying their decline had left farmers and workers suffering.

Wamboka accused National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula of failing to deliver development promises made to Bungoma residents citing unfinished roads and the stalled Bungoma stadium, saying several projects lacked adequate funding despite repeated commitments to voters during the campaigns.

He also questioned Wetang’ula’s political record, citing past controversies and accusing the Speaker of failing to live up to his promises adding that voters should judge leaders by what they deliver, not by speeches alone.

Kabuchai MP Majimbo Kalasinga said the tour had proved that Sifuna’s bid was gaining grassroots support.

“Edwin Sifuna is going for president, nothing else,” he said.

He said supporters contributed small amounts to the campaign, arguing that the movement was being funded by ordinary Kenyans rather than wealthy political backers. He said crowds turned up voluntarily.

Kalasinga also announced that Linda Mwananchi would hold a rally in Homa Bay on August 16 despite local warnings. He said Sifuna had a right to campaign anywhere in Kenya.

He called for peaceful competition and warned against attempts to block the rally or restrict political activity in the region emphasising that Kenya is for everyone, constitutionally, peacefully and equally.

They two vowed to fight for the Linda Mwananchi name.

The Wamboka-Kalasinga push adds momentum to Sifuna’s campaign and pressures opposition leaders to unite before the 2027 election.

World.title: Kindiki defends government's development agenda in Mt Kenya
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki and Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on August 10, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reiterated the government’s commitment to ensure equitable development.

Prof Kindiki said that President William Ruto’s government has initiated many development projects in Mt Kenya to transform livelihoods.

“Am advising the people against being deceived to leave the government to join the opposition where nothing is being provided,” he said.

The Deputy President said the road projects which had stalled have since been revived after the government released Sh176 billion owed to contractors to ensure completion of 6,000km.

He spoke at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on Sunday, where he was the chief guest during celebrations to mark 100 years since the establishment of Gaichanjiru Mission Hospital managed by the Catholic Diocese of Murang'a.

Kindiki, who was accompanied by Cabinet Secretaries Alice Wahome (Lands) and Rebecca Miano (Tourism), said that the government has impacted the region with affordable houses estimated at 180,000 units, modern markets and student hostels that have created employment for hundreds of skilled and unskilled persons.

He said the church has a history of partnering with the government in matters concerning development and empowerment of the less fortunate in the community.

“In Murang’a the government has ensured all the projects that KeRRA under Eng Antony Mwaura was working on are completed to give the locals value for money,” said the DP.

During the event, the President gave Sh10 million for procurement of equipment for the health facility, where more than Sh20 million was raised.

Ruto also gave Sh 50 million and directed the Housing Department to facilitate construction of the hospital's ICU, HDU, theatre and laboratory

Kindiki lauded efforts by Wahome that have seen Murang’a County benefit from Sh27 billion programmes from her ministry.

“Murang’a through her efforts has 27 modern markets, Affordable Housing Programme units, and student hostels, programmes that have engaged hundreds of persons,” he said.

World.title: 6 Egyptian universities rank among world’s top 1,000 in 2026 Shanghai Ranking
World.content:
Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced that six Egyptian universities have been included among the world’s top 1,000 universities in the latest edition of the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), commonly known as the Shanghai Ranking, for 2026.

The ranking evaluated more than 2,500 universities and higher education institutions from countries around the world.

Cairo University maintained its position as Egypt’s top-ranked university for the fifth consecutive year, placing in the 401-500 range globally. Alexandria University and Mansoura University ranked second nationally, both falling within the 601-700 global range.

Ain Shams University and Al-Azhar University were placed in the 701-800 range, while Zagazig University ranked in the 901-1000 range.

Higher Education and Scientific Research Minister and acting Culture Minister Abdelaziz Konsowa praised the performance of Egyptian universities in the 2026 Shanghai Ranking, stressing that the ministry continuously monitors the performance of Egyptian universities in international rankings as an indicator of the competitiveness of higher education and scientific research institutions globally.

The Minister said the continued presence of Egyptian universities in prestigious international rankings reflects the state’s efforts to develop the higher education and scientific research system and strengthen internationalization and competitiveness in line with global standards.

The ranking results also highlighted the strong performance of Egyptian universities in the research output (PUB) indicator. Cairo University led Egyptian universities with a score of 39.1 points, followed by Mansoura University with 32.9, Alexandria University with 31.9, Ain Shams University with 31.2, Al-Azhar University with 29.2, and Zagazig University with 26.5.

Ain Shams University recorded the highest growth rate among Egyptian universities in the indicator measuring research papers published in Nature and Science, while Al-Azhar University nearly doubled its score on the indicator compared with 2023. Alexandria University, meanwhile, demonstrated strong performance in the alumni indicator.

Adel Abdel Ghaffar, the Ministry’s Media Adviser and Official Spokesperson, said the Ministry is continuing its efforts to enhance the competitiveness of Egyptian universities and consolidate Egypt’s position as a leading regional hub for higher education and scientific research.

He added that these efforts include developing the scientific research system, expanding international cooperation, and supporting joint research with high citation rates, thereby increasing opportunities for publication in high-impact international scientific journals.

Abdel Ghaffar added that the continued advancement of Egyptian universities in international rankings reflects their efforts to achieve academic and research excellence.

The Shanghai Ranking is one of the world’s oldest university rankings. It was first published in June 2003 by the Center for World-Class Universities at China’s Shanghai Jiao Tong University and has been updated annually since 2009.

The ranking is based on six key indicators, including Nobel Prizes and Fields Medals awarded to alumni and faculty, highly cited researchers, papers published in Nature and Science, papers indexed in major international scientific databases, and per-capita academic performance.

The ministry also highlighted the importance of the Egyptian Knowledge Bank in providing researchers with extensive scientific and research resources, contributing to the advancement of scientific research, and strengthening the international presence of Egyptian universities, research institutions, and centers.

It also pointed to the role of university ranking teams in monitoring international ranking criteria and improving institutional performance accordingly.

World.title: Bibliotheca Alexandrina hosts sports marathon “A Safe Step… Every Step Makes a Difference”
World.content:
The Bibliotheca Alexandrina hosted on Saturday, August 15, 2026, the “A Safe Step… Every Step Makes a Difference” sports marathon, organized by the Fund for Assistance to Victims of Human Trafficking, affiliated with the Cabinet, in cooperation with the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

The event aimed to raise public awareness of the dangers of human trafficking and promote community participation in combating the crime.

The event was attended by Heba al-Rafaei, acting head of the Bibliotheca Alexandrina’s External Relations and Media Sector, representing Bibliotheca Alexandrina Director Ahmed Zayed; Ambassador Amr Ramadan, chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund for Assistance to Victims of Human Trafficking; Mahmoud Abdel Aziz, representing the Minister of Youth and Sports; Safaa al-Sherif, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Youth and Sports in Alexandria; and Amira Heikal, Deputy Governor of Alexandria.

In her address, al-Rafaei welcomed the guests and marathon participants on behalf of Zayed, stressing that the Bibliotheca Alexandrina’s mission extends beyond preserving heritage and disseminating knowledge to actively contributing to community development and raising public awareness, as a platform for dialogue and education.

She said the library’s hosting of the initiative stems from its belief that knowledge is one of the most powerful tools for addressing societal challenges. She called on young people to educate themselves and learn more about issues related to human trafficking and the various forms of human rights violations and exploitation affecting vulnerable groups.

For his part, Ambassador Ramadan said organizing the first “A Safe Step” activities in cooperation with the Ministry of Youth and Sports represents a model of community cooperation and reinforces the values of participation.

He noted that combating human trafficking requires broad public awareness and concerted efforts by various institutions.

Heikal, meanwhile, expressed appreciation for the Bibliotheca Alexandrina’s role in supporting young people and providing activities and events targeting them, stressing that the event reflects the importance of initiatives aimed at engaging youth and strengthening their participation in community issues.

The event featured a number of accompanying activities, including awareness sessions, interactive games, and competitions, giving an interactive dimension to the awareness messages on combating human trafficking.

The activities concluded with a ceremony honoring the winners of the mini-marathon, followed by official photographs with participants and guests.

World.title: Egypt, Libya chambers seal deal to launch annual industrial fair in April 2027
World.content:
The Federation of Egyptian Industries (FEI) and the General Libyan Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture (GLUCC) have signed a cooperation protocol to organize an annual Egyptian-Libyan industrial integration exhibition in the Libyan city of Benghazi, with its inaugural edition tentatively scheduled for April 2027.

The agreement aims to strengthen industrial, trade and investment cooperation, support partnerships between the two countries’ business communities and open new markets for Egyptian and Libyan products.

The protocol seeks to move Egyptian-Libyan economic relations beyond traditional trade toward a more integrated model based on industrial and investment partnerships, the exchange of expertise and technology, stronger joint value and production chains, and greater use of the countries’ production and logistics capabilities.

It also aims to capitalize on Libya’s strategic position as a gateway to a number of African markets.

Head of the Exhibitions and Small Projects Committee at the Federation of Egyptian Industries Hesham el Gazzar said the protocol would support industrial integration between Egypt and Libya, encourage joint partnerships and investments, facilitate the transfer of technology and expertise, and promote joint projects and integrated value chains.

“The exhibition will connect Egyptian companies and factories with their Libyan counterparts and create direct channels for cooperation between the two business communities, helping increase trade and joint investment and improve the competitiveness of national products,” Gazzar said.

“Targeted sectors include building materials, food, chemical and engineering industries, plastics, wood and furniture, ready-made garments and textiles, leather and footwear, as well as other industries offering promising opportunities for integration and investment in the Libyan market,” Gazzar added.

For his part, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Benghazi Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture Saleh al Obeidi said the future vision for Egyptian-Libyan cooperation was based on combining Egypt’s industrial capabilities with Libya’s strategic location to build an economic platform capable of serving African markets.

Linking Egyptian industry with Libya’s logistics infrastructure could enable Egyptian companies to reach a large consumer base in neighboring countries and African markets, Obeidi said.

World.title: Installation of 5th reactor containment tier starts at El Dabaa nuclear plant
World.content:
Installation of the fifth tier of the reactor building inner containment of the first unit at Egypt’s El Dabaa nuclear power plant has started, the Nuclear Power Plants Authority (NPPA) said on Saturday.

The inner containment structure is a cylindrical structure housing the nuclear reactor and equipment belonging to the plant’s primary circuit. The fifth level consists of 12 prefabricated sections manufactured at the El Dabaa nuclear power plant site.

Each section is 7.5 meters high and weighs between 40 and 45 tons, depending on its structural components, the authority said.

Installation of the fifth tier is expected to be completed within two weeks. The sections will then be assembled to form a complete circular ring of the inner containment structure. A heavy-duty crane with a lifting capacity of 2,200 tons is being used for the work.

A team of specialists with extensive experience in the field is carrying out the installation, with all work being conducted in line with the highest international quality and safety standards.

The work is subject to detailed inspection and testing by NPPA monitoring and supervision teams, following completion of all regulatory procedures and requirements set by the Egyptian Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Authority, ensuring the highest levels of safety, security and quality during installation, the authority said.

NPPA Chairman Sherif Helmy said the start of installation of the fifth tier reflected continued efforts, close coordination and effective cooperation with Russian partner Atomstroyexport, alongside full commitment to the highest standards of quality, safety and nuclear security throughout the project.

“The progress achieved at the El Dabaa nuclear power plant was the result of the professional and dedicated work of NPPA monitoring and supervision teams, as well as installation, engineering and design teams from the project’s Russian general contractor, Atomstroyexport, ensuring the highest levels of quality and safety,” Helmy said.

Vice President of AtomStroyexport and Director of the Dabaa Construction Project Alexey Kononenko said the start of the fifth-level installation marked an important construction milestone for the first unit.

Progress on the structure was the result of the dedicated work of workers, technicians, supervisors, engineers, designers and specialists from various fields involved in the project, as well as effective cooperation with the Egyptian side, the project owner, Kononenko said.

World.title: At least 72 dead, including 18 children, in Zimbabwe ferry disaster
World.content:
Harare, Zimbabwe AP — Eighteen children were among more than 70 people killed when an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe this week, police said Saturday after rescuers recovered more bodies.

The ferry capsized in strong waves on Tuesday. Police said that 26 more bodies had been recovered since then, bringing the death toll to 72.

The aging ferry was traveling from the town of Kariba to rural and fishing communities in the country’s northwest, where roads are damaged and public transportation is scarce. Authorities have not said how many people were aboard or how many remain missing.

In this image taken from a video people are rescued from an overloaded ferry that capsized on Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba on Tuesday, Aug. 11. Maxton Kanhema/AP

Estimates have put the number of passengers as high as 153, while authorities say the ferry’s capacity is 90. Zimbabwe’s disaster management agency has said 77 people were rescued.

Authorities initially said the number of children aboard was unknown because those below ticketing age were not included in passenger estimates. A police list released later showed that 16 of the child victims were aged 10 or younger, with the youngest just 1.

Kariba is the world’s largest human-made lake by volume, created by damming the mighty Zambezi River in the late 1950s and early 1960s. It stretches more than 200 kilometers (124 miles) and is up to 40 kilometers (25 miles) wide in places.

Zimbabwe and Zambia share the lake, with their border running through its middle.

World.title: Israeli military says senior Hezbollah commander killed in strike on southern Lebanon
World.content:
The Israeli military said on Sunday it killed a senior Hezbollah commander, a day after it launched deadly strikes in southern Lebanon.

Abu Hassan Alaa “took part in advancing numerous terror attacks against IDF soldiers… including the launch of explosive drones toward IDF soldiers in southern Lebanon,” the Israeli military said.

A wave of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon on Saturday killed at least 11 people, including women and children, the Lebanese Health Ministry said.

The Israeli prime minister’s office had accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire and said three Israeli soldiers were seriously injured in a Hezbollah attack in southern Lebanon.

On Saturday, the Israeli military said it struck a headquarters of Hezbollah’s elite Radwan force in response, killing what they described as a battalion commander and several others.

World.title: JD Vance and the Trump team keep moving the goalposts on Iran
World.content:
One of the Trump administration’s biggest problems in extracting itself from the Iran war is the list of very absolutist goals that President Donald Trump and his team laid out.

The goals have included complete Iranian surrender, regime change, Iran never getting a nuclear weapon and ending Tehran’s support for its Middle East proxy groups like Hezbollah.

As the war — now in its sixth month — has dragged on, this list of goals has conspicuously shifted and been pared back. And Vice President JD Vance appears to have pared it back recently in a remarkable way, offering the latest indication that the administration might be preparing to settle for less — maybe even a lot less.

Appearing on Fox News on Thursday, Vance was asked how the war might end. And he laid out two goals.

“It’s ensuring that the Gulf countries continue to send oil and gas to the world economy so that we have energy price stability,” he said, adding: “That’s goal number one: Keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country.

“And then, obviously, goal number two is ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon.”

This is not the administration’s old list of goals — and the order Vance placed them in is striking.

When asked about Vance’s comments on Friday, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt maintained that “both goals are equally as important to the president.”

The administration has almost always characterized Iran never getting a nuclear weapon as the overriding concern.

And even if the goals are truly equal in the administration’s mind, including oil and gas prices at all — and not other items — is a notable shift.

In fact, Trump explicitly rejected this as a goal back in May. When asked if he considered Americans’ financial situation when trying to resolve the war, Trump responded, “Not even a little bit.” He signaled that denuclearization was so important that he didn’t factor in anything else.

(Trump echoed that line on Friday, saying he would “never apologize” for Americans paying a little more for gas, given the stakes in Iran.)

I wrote in March about how the administration frequently listed four goals for the war — but how the four goals frequently differed depending upon who was speaking.

Some lists included ending funding for proxy groups, for example, while others did not. Some mentioned destroying Iran’s missile infrastructure, while others omitted that. Some mentioned getting rid of Iran’s air force and navy, but others only mentioned the navy.

It was like the administration was workshopping the list in real time.

But the key point here is that none of those lists included keeping oil and gas prices low in the United States.

And given the Strait of Hormuz was open before the war started, that particular goal could just be read as a return to the pre-war status quo — with denuclearization being the only goal that would represent a new achievement.

Indeed, the new emphasis on low gas prices from some in the administration seems like the latest sign of relaxing the goals to prepare for a conclusion to the war that comes up well shy of Trump’s initial aims.

By May, it became clear the administration was no longer going to emphasize certain goals.

By June, the Trump administration entered into a memorandum of understanding with Iran that barely mentioned previously central US goals.

And for the last two-plus months, Trump has been saying things that sounded a lot like he might scale back his nuclear demands.

While the administration previously emphasized Iran turning over its enriched uranium, Trump’s spoken about how perhaps enough damage was done to its nuclear program and its nuclear materials are buried too far underground to be accessed. The president has also talked about how the US government could simply monitor from space to make sure Iran didn’t try to retrieve them.

He’s even claimed that Iran was already denuclearized.

In other words, Trump sounded a lot like a guy who knew he might not be able to cow Iran into accepting a really restrictive nuclear deal.

His administration talking about energy prices as “goal number one” — even if Trump isn’t — would fit neatly with this progression away from the hard-and-fast goals that the administration set out to achieve.

If a return to the pre-war status quo really is “goal number one” right now, that says a lot about how little this war has accomplished.

World.title: All-powerful Trump tells America, ‘Nothing bad can happen’
World.content:
Just one of the wild actions and comments on Donald Trump’s manic Monday would rank among the most notorious things another president ever did.

By close of business, Trump had taken strides toward the presidency he’s always wanted: one of unfiltered authority flowing from the presidential Sharpie, shredding traditional institutions and providing a platform for demagoguery.

Often, the round-the-clock cacophony from the White House seems expressly designed to stifle public comprehension of each individual act planned to irrevocably change the country and the world.

This was certainly the case on a day that fulfilled some core goals of the Trump base but also helped to explain the plunging presidential approval ratings that have Republicans looking with dread toward the midterm elections.

It all started when one of the president’s former personal lawyers, now Appeals Court Judge Emil Bove, swore in another of the president’s former personal lawyers, Todd Blanche, as attorney general.

This was peak Trump. Nine years after the president asked James Comey for loyalty — as the fired former FBI chief told it — one of his ultimate loyalists was on Monday installed in a Senate-confirmed position at the pinnacle of US justice.

Blanche was with Trump in some of his darkest moments as he faced multiple criminal and civil charges before winning back the White House. Some Trump subordinates, like former Attorney General Pam Bondi, stumbled when striving to prove their loyalty. But Blanche has already demonstrated fealty — one reason his critics fear him and wonder whether he’ll act a spiritual successor to Trump’s McCarthyite lawyer Roy Cohn.

As Blanche was clapped by staff back into his agency, more of the president’s men gathered by the Resolute Desk. He was about to act on a feeling he’s harbored even longer than his quest to make the DOJ his boutique law firm.

Trump then signed an executive order aimed at reducing the number of childhood vaccines. And he administered a fresh dose of unscientific falsehoods, baselessly claiming vaccines cause autism and that little children had had inoculations the size of soda bottles poured into their bodies. At one point, he suggested that the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine could be “quite lethal” — amid a year when the US has recorded the most measles cases in more than a quarter-century. It was hard not to get flashbacks to his erratic Covid-19 pandemic news conferences.

But America’s most powerful public health official and vaccine skeptic, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., insisted: “This is what gold-standard science means.”

Moments later, another longtime norm fractured

Trump confirmed he’d recently spoken to new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, but denied a Wall Street Journal report they’d had multiple conversations. The president has left no doubt he wants Warsh to lower interest rates. “If it was up to him, it would be different, but he has a board,” Trump said, raising doubts about the central bank’s independence.

The president also weighed in on the triumph of progressive and democratic socialist candidates in Democratic primaries ahead of the midterm elections: “We have jihadists being elected all over the place.”

The president’s latest inflammatory comment about Muslim candidates appears to herald a viciously negative fall campaign. He didn’t specify who he was talking about, but his remark came a week after Abdul El-Sayed won the Michigan Democratic Senate primary.

When he turned to Iran, the president showed how the once-intricate US foreign policy process has ceded to the wish-casting of the commander in chief who declared a war won after a few days that is now in its sixth month. And he claimed the Strait of Hormuz, an oil exporting choke point effectively controlled by Iran, is “opened now.” The Windward Maritime Intelligence Operations Center said Monday that only seven vessels had crossed the strait in the previous 24 hours. Before the war, the waterway often saw more than 100 ships a day.

Each of these examples show how Trump has degraded the institutions of US government and purged them of experts, bureaucrats and officials who don’t share his idiosyncratic worldview.

Many Trump supporters argue that he’s making good on his vow to dismantle a corrupt administrative state that has long thwarted conservative presidents. Others promote the idea of an all-powerful presidency and subscribe to legal theories that every government agency must bow to the chief executive’s vision.

Trump runs everything

In some ways, the maelstrom of business across the Oval Office desk Monday mirrors the deeply centralized decision-making process developed for years by the future president at the Trump Organization, where he was the sole source of authority. But Trump’s critics see his hands-on style as the behavior of a wannabe authoritarian and argue his hunch-driven style of leadership is a recipe for disaster.

It’s hard to make a case that Trump’s approach is working for anyone outside his most loyal support base, despite his claim in an interview with Punchbowl News last week that “a lot of people are saying I’m one of the greatest presidents ever.”

In a recent CNN/SSRS poll, only 21 percent of Americans said Trump’s military action in Iran had helped the US. Many analysts believe he’s led the US into a stalemate against a much weaker nation.

His crusade to dominate the Justice Department is one of the personal fixations — along with his monument-building program — that help explain why a record-high 73 percent of US adults said in that same CNN survey that he hasn’t paid enough attention to the country’s most important problems.

And according to polling from the health policy nonprofit KFF, an 81 percent majority of US adults say they are confident that MMR vaccines are safe for children. A small sector of Trump’s base, however, has long bought into the anti-vaccine movement.

Some of the institutionalists who Trump disdains warned on Monday evening that his increasingly unchecked presidency is dangerous.

“It is simply astonishing that this administration would continue to respond to ongoing measles outbreaks and the return of other vaccine-preventable diseases by playing politics with children’s lives,” said Dr. Richard Besser, president and CEO of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and former acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

David Axelrod, who served as a counselor to Barack Obama, told CNN’s Erin Burnett that a president’s words “can send armies marching and markets tumbling.” But they can “also jeopardize people’s health because the president has enormous sway. … It’s really, really dangerous.”

But Trump is beyond listening. Explaining his vaccine policy, he seemed both to encapsulate his attitude to unchecked power and to tempt fate.

“Nothing bad can happen from what we’re doing,” he said. “Nothing bad can happen.”

World.title: Liberia: Herbalist Jailed for Frightening Woman Into Paying US7,200
World.content:
Sixty-year-old man accused of exploiting fear, traditional beliefs and threats in alleged death-scare scheme

Mobrovia-“I was hired to kill you,” was the alleged warning that turned fear into cash, that later landed 61-year-old Saah Fayiah Jr., alias Alahaji Bamba, in prison.

Liberian police say Fayiah allegedly posed as a traditional herbalist and convinced a woman, Pauline S. Zaza, a resident of Lower Margibi County, that her life was in immediate danger, before allegedly collecting US$7,200 from her through a series of demands for spiritual sacrifices.

According to a police charge sheet dated August 13, Fayiah allegedly told Madan Zaza that an unidentified man had paid him US$5,000 to kill her.

Police say Fayiah further claimed Zaza had only three days to live.

The alleged threat set in motion what investigators describe as a calculated scheme that allegedly exploited Zaza’s fear and belief in traditional spiritual intervention.

THREE-DAY DEATH WARNING

According to investigators, Zaza initially responded by sending Fayiah LD$5,000 after allegedly being told that her life was under threat.

Police say Fayiah later traveled to Fendell, where he allegedly performed what Zaza believed was a spiritual ritual.

Investigators allege that the encounter intensified the woman’s fears.

Fayiah allegedly told Zaza that spiritual forces were threatening her and that money was needed to perform sacrifices.

Among the alleged demands were funds to purchase a cow, goat and chicken.

What began with an alleged death threat would eventually result in thousands of United States dollars allegedly changing hands.

Police say Zaza ultimately paid Fayiah US$7,200 in several instalments.

But investigators allege the demands did not stop there.

ANOTHER US$3,000 DEMANDED

According to the police account, Fayiah subsequently demanded another US$3,000.

Zaza allegedly could not raise the entire amount.

Police say she managed to provide US$2,000.

Then came another demand.

Investigators alleged that on August 11, Fayiah requested an additional US$100 and instructed Zaza to meet him in Clara Town.

But this time, police say, investigators were waiting.

Fayiah was reportedly arrested during the planned meeting after Zaza had already complained to authorities.

THE WITNESS WHO FOLLOWED THE TRAIL

The investigation reportedly includes the account of Solomon Grant, a witness who told police he accompanied Zaza to meetings with Fayiah on six occasions.

Grant reportedly said Zaza believed Fayiah was a native doctor and sought his assistance because of the alleged threat against her life.

His account could become important if prosecutors seek to establish how the alleged scheme operated and how Fayiah allegedly maintained Zaza’s confidence in his claims.

FAYIAH DENIES THE ACCUSATION

Fayiah has reportedly denied the allegations.

According to police, he told investigators that his dealings with Zaza were connected to a land dispute and an effort to help her become wealthy.

He reportedly denied threatening Zaza or deceiving her into surrendering money.

But investigators say they found no evidence that Fayiah was a legitimate herbalist and no evidence supporting his alleged claim that someone had hired him to kill Zaza.

That finding raises a more troubling question at the heart of the case, how much money can fear extract from a vulnerable person when the person creating the fear presents himself as the one capable of providing salvation.

WHEN FEAR BECOMES A BUSINESS

The case highlights a sensitive issue in Liberia: the exploitation of traditional beliefs and fear for financial gain.

For many Liberians, traditional medicine and spiritual practices remain part of everyday life.

But police say the Fayiah case involves something fundamentally different, the alleged use of a fabricated threat of death to obtain money.

If proven in court, the allegations would suggest that the supposed danger was not merely a threat from an unknown attacker.

It was allegedly the foundation of the entire scheme.

The alleged message was simple, pay, or die. And each new demand allegedly came with another reason why payment was necessary.

CHARGED WITH THEFT OF PROPERTY

Fayiah has been charged with Theft of Property under Section 15.51 of Liberia’s Revised Penal Law and was forwarded to the Monrovia City Court on Friday, August 14.

The charge follows a police investigation triggered by Zaza’s complaint and culminating in Fayiah’s arrest.

He remains in custody as the legal process proceeds.

The prosecution will ultimately have to establish in court that the alleged payments were obtained through conduct that satisfies the elements of the criminal offense.

The police charge sheet represents allegations, not a judicial finding of guilt.

A CASE BEYOND US$7,200

At face value, the case is about US$7,200.

But the allegations raise a much larger concern.

If someone can allegedly convince another person that an assassin has been paid to kill her, and then allegedly position himself as the only person capable of preventing that death, where does spiritual counselling end and criminal exploitation begin?

And when fear becomes the currency, how many victims remain silent because they are embarrassed to admit they believed the threat.

For Zaza, police intervention allegedly ended the cycle on August 11.

For Fayiah, however, the next battle will be fought not through rituals or spiritual claims, but in a courtroom.

There, prosecutors will have to prove whether the frightening story that allegedly extracted thousands of dollars from a terrified woman was a genuine warning, or a carefully constructed deception designed to make money.

Fayiah has been remanded behind bars by Monrovia City Court Judge Ben Barco and he remains presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Liberia National Tourism Authority and Wode Maya Conclude Two-Day Masterclass with Nearly 200 Creators
World.content:
A two-day masterclass led by Ghanaian content creator Wode Maya has concluded in Liberia, bringing together nearly 200 content creators for practical sessions on content creation, digital storytelling and the growing role of creators in promoting Liberia.

The masterclass, hosted by the Liberia National Tourism Authority (LNTA) at the Liberia Learning Center in Paynesville, was designed to equip members of Liberia’s creative community with knowledge and practical insights to strengthen their work and reach wider audiences through digital platforms.

The first day focused on content creators in general, with sessions exploring the fundamentals of creating engaging content, effective storytelling, audience building, personal branding and strategies for growing a presence across social media and other digital platforms.

The second day placed a particular focus on travel vloggers and creators, looking at how compelling digital stories can help showcase Liberia’s destinations, culture, heritage, people and tourism experiences to audiences both locally and internationally.

Speaking during the masterclass, Wode Maya stressed the importance of authenticity, consistency and purpose in content creation, encouraging participants to see their platforms as more than just spaces for entertainment.

“Content creators have the power to change the way people see a country. Liberia has so many stories, places and experiences that the world needs to discover, and creators have a responsibility to tell those stories in an authentic and engaging way,” Wode Maya said.

He encouraged creators to take advantage of the opportunities offered by digital platforms to build their personal brands while using their influence to contribute to the promotion of Liberia’s tourism potential.

Participants also explored the importance of authenticity and consistency in content creation, as well as the potential for creators to contribute to Liberia’s tourism promotion by presenting the country through fresh and engaging perspectives.

For participants, the masterclass provided an opportunity to gain new skills, exchange ideas and learn from an experienced content creator with a wide audience across Africa and beyond.

“This masterclass reminded us that the stories we tell can go beyond our individual platforms. We have an opportunity to use our creativity to showcase Liberia, highlight what makes our country unique and connect our stories with audiences beyond our borders,” said Maureen Jennifer Davies, a participant in the masterclass.

The programme also featured a panel discussion bringing together voices from Liberia’s creative space. Panelists shared their experiences, discussed opportunities and challenges within the industry, and examined how stronger collaboration between creators and the tourism sector could contribute to the promotion of Liberia.

The discussions highlighted the growing importance of digital storytelling in tourism promotion, particularly as social media and other digital platforms increasingly influence how people discover destinations, explore travel experiences and decide where to visit.

The masterclass comes at a time when digital platforms are playing an increasingly important role in how destinations are discovered, experienced and perceived, placing content creators at the centre of conversations about Liberia’s image and tourism potential.

With nearly 200 creators participating, the two-day programme not only provided a platform for learning and knowledge-sharing but also underscored the growing potential of Liberia’s creative community to help tell the country’s tourism story and take it to audiences around the world.

World.title: BCHT, Administration And Caucus Dedicate Baryatah Clinic and Bridge in District Two
World.content:
GBARGA, Bong County — At long last, Bong County Health Team, in collaboration with the County Administration and Legislative Caucus, has finally dedicated the newly completed Baryatah Clinic and Bridge in Jorquelleh District #2, with officials describing the projects as significant investments in healthcare delivery and road connectivity.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The Bridge and Clinic projects were allocated under the 2018–2019 County Social Development Fund and national Budget Respectively through the efforts of former District Two Representative now Senator Prince Kermue Moye Sr. However, both projects faced significant delays over the years due to what many described as political interplays.
